title: Artifact byte checksums
text: API: md5 gives the exact contract. artifact_checksum::md5 computes the sixteen MD5 digest bytes for a byte slice. The artifact parser uses this legacy checksum for its Z-card check. The Z card is the artifact checksum record. It does not select repository content identities. SHA-1 and SHA3 remain in content_hash. Structural parsing has its own explicit limits and validation rules. Md5Checksum::new starts an owned computation. update appends the complete slice, including zero bytes and bytes outside UTF-8. Empty updates do nothing. finish consumes the computation and returns [u8; 16]. Each value has fixed memory use and can be interleaved with other computations. No input copy, file access or process-global state is required. Slice lengths bound each call. The caller chooses how much data to supply. There is no artifact size policy or cancellation mechanism in this byte primitive. use gossil::artifact_checksum::{md5, Md5Checksum}; let mut checksum = Md5Checksum::new(); checksum.update(b"a"); checksum.update(b"bc"); assert_eq!(checksum.finish(), md5(b"abc"));

title: Artifact byte checksums
text: The inspected Fossil mirror is b3a1c8efb2731dffbd5cc38c58ac349746de6da6. The native build reports 7e8ecf0ce4a3c05aa39de7ffe2828d23e334efe446ef2387e09f205ef00b2227. In src/manifest.c, verify_z_card hashes the bytes before the final 35-byte Z card through md5sum_init, md5sum_step_text and md5sum_finish. This module supplies that checksum operation. It does not inspect a Z card. The byte result maps to md5sum_blob in src/md5.c. The incremental operations map to the positive-length and zero-length byte behavior of md5sum_step_text. Rust ownership replaces the native shared context and overwritten static result. The consuming finish requires a fresh value for another computation. It does not reproduce the native implicit reset. Negative lengths and C string scanning are excluded. md5sum_step_blob needs no separate Rust adapter because slices already describe bytes and length. Excluded native functions are md5sum_current_state, md5sum_file and md5sum_test. md5sum_current_state sums words of the internal context for troubleshooting. Its two callers in vfile.c are commented out. It is not a snapshot of the MD5 digest. The native command and filesystem behaviors, repository R-card aggregation, ETags and all artifact producers remain outside this module. Native MD5Init, MD5Update, MD5Final, MD5Transform and DigestToBase16 are not translated into Rust here. The implementation uses RustCrypto’s exact-pinned md-5 version 0.10.6. This version shares the existing digest 0.10 dependency with SHA-2. The lockfile records its registry checksum. Its versioned documentation describes the API used here. RustCrypto’s current documentation identifies legacy interoperability as the purpose of MD5. This module adds no identity or security policy and forwards no computation to C.

title: Artifact parser
text: API: parse_artifact and parse_artifact_with_usage give the exact contracts. The artifact module parses all eight Fossil structural artifact types with explicit resource limits. The types are manifest, cluster, control, wiki, ticket, attachment, technote and forum. A card is a record in the artifact byte format. The parser takes bytes and returns an owned result with read-only access to parsed fields. It keeps the original input, including any signature envelope. It does not require valid UTF-8.

title: Artifact parser
text: Call parse_artifact(input, limits, dates).await with a ParseLimits value chosen for the calling operation. Set each field explicitly, including input_bytes, cards, owned_bytes and entries. All four fields have type usize. The byte fields count bytes, and the other fields count cards and list entries. There is no default policy. The owned-byte limit counts logical charges for retained input, encoded tokens, copies and list entries. Allocations use fallible reservation. A resource failure is separate from malformed input, checksum mismatch and a date-provider failure.

title: Artifact parser
text: For several artifacts in one operation, call parse_artifact_with_usage(input, limits, dates).await. It returns the same parsed result with a ParseUsage value on success. The original parse_artifact function delegates to this implementation and returns only the parsed result. ParseUsage reports charges against each limit. input_bytes counts the full raw input, including a recognized signature envelope. cards counts nonzero card markers consumed by the structural loop, including Z and repeated empty P cards. A trailing zero marker consumes its delimiter without adding a card. Body newlines and envelope lines do not add cards. owned_bytes reports all charged bytes, including retained raw input, copies, encoded token lengths charged before decoding, and the size of inserted list entries. The counters report logical charges against ParseLimits; they do not measure every physical Rust allocator byte. This charge can exceed the decoded output length. It also includes allocations for tokens later discarded, such as reserved file paths. entries counts list insertions; empty P cards add none. Subtract successful usage from the operation’s remaining limits before the next call. Each call checks those remaining limits before its charged allocations. Usage is returned only on success. A caller that needs an atomic operation must stop on any error and discard its operation state. The parser does not maintain the aggregate budget or remember earlier failures. The API example parses a cluster and subtracts all four successful charges from a caller-owned budget. The private recording library borrows one parser work ledger across its complete repository operation. Other callers remain responsible for their own aggregate accounting.

title: Artifact parser
text: Implement DateProvider on the operation’s selected SQLite/libSQL owner. The local storage guide explains transaction ownership. Its asynchronous julianday method can borrow a transaction. It receives an optional raw token already truncated by the parser at its native C-string boundary, and returns an optional Julian day. A NULL result acts as zero and fails date validation. Provider execution errors retain their original cause. A constant date adapter can isolate grammar tests, but it cannot qualify date compatibility. The result exposes decoded comments and users, manifest files and parents, tags, ticket fields and cluster members. It also exposes attachment fields, wiki and forum fields, body bytes and converted dates. D cards carry artifact dates, and E cards carry event dates. Their raw date tokens remain available. Callers cannot construct or mutate a validated result through this API.

title: Artifact parser
text: The port follows Fossil manifest.c:467-1153 and its eight allowed/required card masks at lines 129-138. The pinned Fossil UUID is 7e8ecf0ce4a3c05aa39de7ffe2828d23e334efe446ef2387e09f205ef00b2227. Fossil’s source is copyright D. Richard Hipp under the Simplified BSD License. The parser checks the exact MD5 before decoding a recognized final Z record. It strips recognized PGP and SSH envelopes for parsing and checksum purposes. Envelope stripping does not verify a signature’s authenticity. The pinned card matrix requires Z even for manifests. R validates hexadecimal syntax. Repository file checksum verification belongs to storage. Tokens stop at space, LF or raw NUL. Each card consumes tokens as its native branch does. A raw NUL can be an intermediate delimiter in some cards. It is not subject to a blanket acceptance rule. Decoded tokens retain bytes after an escaped NUL, together with the length visible to C consumers. A zero card marker ends the native card loop after consuming its space or LF delimiter. Parsing succeeds only if that cursor reaches the end and the earlier cards satisfy the type rules. Unread bytes after the marker still fail. The W scanner uses unsigned 32-bit modular arithmetic and the native new < old overflow branch. It checks the remaining input before copying body bytes. Decimal suffixes and empty digit sequences follow the source branch. Manifest file paths use the legacy nonstrict rules. Paths must be nonempty and have no empty, dot or dot-dot slash-separated components. Unicode and backslash restrictions are not imposed. Reserved filenames are suppressed after comparison with the last retained filename. The parser retains repeated empty P cards, native type inference, tag ordering, forum postconditions and the historical technote P-before-N exception. Attachment basenames follow the compiled platform’s directory separator rule. Windows behavior remains unqualified.

title: Byte digests and packed blobs
text: API: pack gives the exact contract. The library has Fossil byte digests and packed-blob operations. Packing adds a capacity header to compressed bytes. These primitives do not select a repository hash policy or store content. The runner and these primitives share a crate. CLI integration remains separate work. Legacy MD5 checksums have a separate artifact checksum module. The artifact parser uses that module for Z-card validation. The checksum module does not select repository content identities.

title: Byte digests and packed blobs
text: use gossil::{compression, content_hash}; let digest = content_hash::sha1(b"abc"); assert_eq!(digest.len(), 20); let packed = compression::pack(b"abc", -1).unwrap(); assert_eq!(compression::unpack(&packed, 3).unwrap(), compression::Unpacked::Bytes(b"abc".to_vec())); In the example, -1 selects the default compression level, and 3 limits decoded output to three bytes. sha1(input: &[u8]) returns [u8; 20]. pack(input: &[u8], level: i32) returns Result , BlobError>. unpack(input: &[u8], max_output: usize) returns Result . See the runner prerequisites for actual tool setup.

title: Byte digests and packed blobs
text: The port follows Fossil Git revision b3a1c8efb2731dffbd5cc38c58ac349746de6da6. The source surfaces are src/blob.c:1372–1535, src/sha1.c:185–201, and src/sha3.c:385–468,591–606,622–679, and the SHA1DC initialization in src/sha1hard.c:1327–1342. content_hash::sha1 accepts arbitrary bytes and returns twenty digest bytes. SHA1DC detects known SHA1 collision attacks. It preserves Fossil’s collision detection and safe-hash defaults. For a known collision attack, it returns the mitigated digest. The byte helper ignores the separate collision indication, as sha1sum_blob does. It does not return the ordinary vulnerable digest for those inputs. content_hash::sha3 accepts each width from 128 through 512 in steps of 32. It returns the corresponding binary digest, or None for an unsupported width. content_hash::hex renders bytes as lowercase hexadecimal. SHA3 uses Fossil’s width-dependent capacity and its 0x06 and 0x80 padding. The small adapter handles byte absorption, padding and extraction in explicit little-endian lane order. The maintained keccak crate supplies the permutation. A shorter digest is not a truncated standard-width hash. The four standard widths use FIPS-202 padding. The other widths preserve Fossil’s extensions. compression::pack accepts zlib levels -1 and zero through nine. Level -1 selects the backend default. compression::pack_two compresses the concatenated slices at level nine, as Fossil does. Neither operation allocates a concatenated input buffer. The compressed representation can differ between backends. A packed blob contains a four-byte unsigned big-endian capacity followed by a zlib stream. The capacity is an upper bound on decoded bytes. A larger header than the actual output is valid. Bytes following the first complete zlib stream are ignored. Invalid checksums, incomplete streams and output exceeding the header produce errors. compression::unpack accepts a caller-selected limit. It rejects a header above that limit before decoding, then checks each output chunk against the header. Output grows through fallible reservations. The caller sets the limit. The format has no additional fixed small cap. Encoding rejects lengths above the unsigned 32-bit header range. C overflow and undefined behavior are not ported. Inputs of at most four bytes produce Unpacked::NoPayload. A caller that replaces an existing buffer must leave its existing buffer contents unchanged for that result. A successfully decoded empty stream produces Unpacked::Bytes with an empty vector. These outcomes differ. Fossil’s diagnostic test-uncompress ignores the C function’s error return, so CLI exit zero does not prove successful decoding. Allocation and compression errors retain their underlying causes. Digest results have a fixed small size. Compressed input and output remain caller-owned. The API does not define database, filesystem, publication or privacy behavior.

title: CLI reference
text: The gossil executable initializes empty repositories, opens native checkouts and has three delta file diagnostics. The prepared source also has a glob diagnostic, with a focused source checkpoint. This source checkout also has explicit add and tracked status, plus scope selection and private recording and complete recorded ancestry. gos is an alias for gossil, and v is an alias for vcs. Each diagnostic runs without a repository. Run it from this source checkout with just gossil, which builds and runs the executable through Cargo. Cargo may print build messages on stderr. Command Arguments Successful output vcs test-delta-create ORIGIN TARGET DELTA Writes DELTA; no stdout vcs test-delta-apply ORIGIN DELTA TARGET Writes TARGET; no stdout vcs test-delta FILE1 FILE2 Prints ok and a newline vcs test-glob PATTERN STRING ... Prints SQL, patterns and match indices; prepared source just gossil vcs test-delta-create ORIGIN TARGET DELTA just gossil vcs test-delta-apply ORIGIN DELTA TARGET just gossil vcs test-delta FILE1 FILE2 Replace capitalized arguments with file paths. The commands accept exactly the number of paths shown. Each diagnostic requires the vcs or v group. Neither executable has help subcommands. File data comes from paths and goes to paths. Stdin and stdout do not carry it.

title: CLI reference
text: just gossil vcs init --admin-user alice --date-override '2026-11-18 12:34:56' NEW_REPOSITORY just gossil vcs new --sha1 ANOTHER_NEW_REPOSITORY Initialization accepts exactly one destination. Both executable names and both group names support init and its new alias. The destination must be new; existing files, symlinks and SQLite recovery sidecars are refused. Option Behavior --admin-user USERNAME, -A USERNAME Set the initial administrator --date-override DATETIME Set the root date; default now --sha1 Use SHA1 for the initial root and native hash policy --help, -h Print initialization help and exit successfully -- Treat following arguments as literal destination names Long value options also accept --name=value. Without an explicit administrator, the command selects the first nonempty value from GOSSIL_USER, USER, LOGNAME and USERNAME, in that order. If all are absent or empty, it uses root. No preference file is read or created. Administrator bytes reach native validation unchanged; the storage API requires valid UTF-8. Repository filenames retain native bytes, including names beginning with file:. Dates must be UTF-8 and accepted by the native date provider. The receipt prints the committed project and server identifiers, administrator and initial remote-access password. Keep that password private. A receipt write failure returns status 1 after commit and leaves the repository initialized. Other initialization failures also return status 1. Initialization help returns 0. The command creates an empty native root without a checkout. Templates, project display fields and global preference options are unsupported and rejected before creation. Use the separate open command below to register or reopen one empty-root checkout. The scope and commit commands below record private history. The bounded timeline and log commands below expose the recorded_timeline API. Revision selection and broader history commands remain deferred. An already installed mini-VCS preview has a separate command contract. This guide does not record a new installation or publication.

title: CLI reference
text: First registration binds one existing directory to the initial empty root. Reopen also admits the supported private history written by the library. The locator is an owner-local lookup file at ROOT/.gossil/checkout.json. Neither operation selects files, creates file history or restores working files. The source supports open and locator recovery. Installation and publication require separate delivery evidence. just gossil vcs open --repository PATH --checkout ID --root ROOT Option Behavior --repository PATH Required existing local repository database --checkout ID Required exact checkout ID, with UTF-8 text --root ROOT Existing directory for explicit first registration or same-root reopen Options take separate values and each may appear once, in any order. Unknown options, duplicate options, positional arguments and missing values fail. Open has no --help, --register, --name=value or default repository selection. Use either gossil or gos, with either vcs or v. For first registration, create the repository separately with vcs init, then supply --root. Open requires an existing database and never creates one. The root can contain ordinary files and nested Git repositories. Their bytes remain unselected and unchanged. Native VCS open requires no issue, project or author initialization. It does not grant Gest project authority. The native library admits catalog4 with exactly zero or one registration and the supported tracking, scope and private recording history. Catalog1, unrelated file history and a second registration are outside this command. The storage guide defines those catalog formats. Native admission checks the repository and owner binding, canonical root, device/inode and complete supported state. The locator cannot replace those checks. See native storage for identity, root and resource limits.

title: CLI reference
text: For an existing registration, omit --root and invoke open from its root or a nested directory: cd ROOT /path/to/gos v open --repository PATH --checkout ID Use an absolute database path when changing directories. Open searches from the canonical current directory toward the filesystem root and stops at the nearest .gossil marker. It does not skip an incomplete, unsafe or conflicting marker to select an ancestor. Explicit repository and checkout flags must agree with both the locator and admitted database registration. An explicit --root preserves that exact requested root. If discovery finds a marker at an ancestor, first registration refuses rather than reusing the ancestor checkout. Repeating open with the same root and an existing valid locator reuses the admitted registration and syncs the locator directory. If checkout.json is missing, rootless open can reconstruct it from the exact existing registration. When no marker exists, run from the registered root itself. Recovery authenticates exactly one matching registration and preserves its identities, native keys and registration count. It allocates no checkout and repairs no database state. An incomplete marker prevents a new registration through --root. Malformed or conflicting locators remain conflicts and are never replaced.

title: CLI reference
text: Open loads inherited Gest configuration from the invocation directory, even when --root names another directory. Explicit repository flags do not bypass configuration checks. Layers merge in this order, with later values taking precedence: The file named by GEST_CONFIG, or the platform configuration directory’s gest/config.toml when that variable is absent. Each ancestor from the filesystem root through the canonical invocation directory, reading .config/gest.toml then .gest.toml in each directory. Environment values with the GEST_ prefix. Double underscores separate nested keys, and key names become lowercase. A usable absolute storage.data_dir explicitly selects gossil.db inside that directory. Its canonical existing database must match --repository. The exact uppercase GEST_STORAGE__DATA_DIR accepts an absolute native-byte path without UTF-8 loss. An effective relative path is not an explicit selection and does not revive a value from an earlier configuration layer. Malformed TOML, unreadable configuration files and invalid table or value types fail before marker or database mutation. A configured database.url or database.host is unsupported and also fails, including with explicit CLI flags. These errors do not print the configured provider value. Typed I/O, TOML and JSON causes remain inspectable through the retained error chain. Configuration supplies no implicit database creation or fallback through an incomplete marker. The configuration adapter retains Gest’s MIT attribution at pinned source eaf821b19c3cf75b99d22e1cc70e0eff4a3562a8 in src/checkout_config.rs.

title: CLI reference
text: The locator contains exactly version, repository_path_hex, repository_id and checkout_id. Version is integer 1. The path is the actual absolute Unix database filename, encoded as lowercase hexadecimal without losing native bytes. The repository ID is the admitted 40-character lowercase identity. The checkout ID names the real persisted registration. Reading is bounded to 65536 bytes, including whitespace. Parsing rejects unknown or duplicate fields, trailing data and malformed versions, identities or path encodings. Decoded database paths are bounded to 16384 bytes and must be absolute and NUL-free. Locator checkout IDs are bounded to 8192 UTF-8 bytes. The native registration API separately requires its smaller 1024-byte ID limit. The marker and locator must belong to the effective user and must not be symlinks. A marker must be a directory without group or other write permission. A locator must be a regular file without group or other permissions. New marker directories use mode 0700, and new temporary files use mode 0600. Open refuses unsafe objects and preserves their bytes and permissions.

title: CLI reference
text: First registration prepares complete bounded locator bytes in an exclusively created temporary file inside the marker directory. It flushes and syncs that file before changing the database. After checked registration commit, it publishes through a hard link that cannot overwrite checkout.json, then syncs the marker directory. An identical existing locator also requires directory sync. There is no replacement or copy fallback when linking fails. Failure phase Preserved result and next action Preflight No new registration was committed by this locator attempt; resolve the input or namespace conflict CommittedUnpublished Registration remains committed; retry without --root from the registered root to reconstruct the missing locator DurabilityUnconfirmed Locator is present but directory durability is unconfirmed; preserve it and retry the same admitted open Published Locator is present and its directory was synced; owned temporary cleanup failed Cleanup targets only this attempt’s temporary pathname with its recorded identity. Unrelated crash leftovers and replacement objects are preserved. Callers must keep the namespace stable. The contract does not promise atomic filesystem/database commit or protection against hostile concurrent replacement. After all durable locator pins are lost, recovery cannot prove historical identity against malicious database substitution. Success prints Opened checkout ID at ROOT (repository REPOSITORY_ID, head HEAD) and returns status 0. HEAD is the shared head, which stays at the empty root when the library records private history. Failures return status 1 with a diagnostic on stderr. Locator diagnostics name their publication phase. Internal error categories do not change this process exit status. A receipt write failure can occur after successful publication. It preserves the committed registration and locator, so a failed command does not imply that nothing committed.

title: CLI reference
section: Add explicit paths and inspect pending additions
text: This source checkout provides vcs add and vcs status at the initial root or an admitted private recorded head. Add records tracking metadata. Status lists all tracked paths, their pending or recorded state, and their actual scope. Use the separate scope and commit commands below to select scopes and record files. First, use vcs open to publish or recover the locator. Then run these commands from the registered checkout root or one of its descendants: /path/to/gos v add --repository /absolute/history.gossil --checkout work --path notes/plan.md --path notes/review.md /path/to/gos v status --repository /absolute/history.gossil --checkout work Both --repository and --checkout are required exactly once. Repeat --path PATH for each file; there are no positional path lists. Paths are exact UTF-8 names relative to the registered root, regardless of the invocation directory. Status accepts no paths. Neither command accepts --json, --root, scope switches or recursive selection. Both executable names and both group aliases use this grammar. Add accepts existing regular files only. It rejects absolute paths, empty components, . and .., backslashes, duplicate paths within a batch, case aliases, symlinks and special files. On macOS, paths must also be ASCII. This implementation rejects non-ASCII paths because their filesystem name comparisons have not been qualified. The .gossil namespace, selected database, SQLite sidecars and known hard-link aliases are protected. Parent directories and leaves are opened without following symlinks, and their identities are rechecked before commit. Keep the filesystem namespace stable during the command; these checks do not promise protection against hostile concurrent replacement. The CLI bounds the complete tracked inventory and each batch to 4096 paths. Each path has at most 4096 bytes and 128 components. Add temporarily captures files to validate the batch. It limits those initial captures to 64 MiB of working bytes and uses a 64 KiB read buffer. The final recheck temporarily holds a second copy of one file alongside those captures, so captured bytes can total 128 MiB. These bounds exclude other process allocations. Native admission has separate finite bounds. If any bound is exceeded, the command returns an error. Add persists tracking metadata only. Earlier additions remain tracked across batches and reopen. A successful batch with new paths advances pending_version once; an existing-only batch validates and rereads its inputs without changing rows or counters. A failed batch rolls back its metadata changes. Working files are never written. Temporary reads do not create a stored content snapshot, a check-in or a recording receipt. Both commands print the complete tracked inventory in pathname order: Tracked paths (A: pending addition, R: recorded): A unselected "notes/plan.md" A unselected "notes/review.md" Each row starts with A for a pending addition or R for a recorded path. A tab separates the state, scope and path. Scope is unselected, shared or private; the path uses Rust debug-string syntax with quotes and escapes. A selected scope assigns a path to shared or owner-local private history. unselected means that no choice has been stored. Empty status prints only the heading. Status does not discover untracked files or report modified, missing, removed or renamed files. It does not reread working file content. An output failure returns status 1, and an add may already have committed. New paths have unselected scope. Add grants no recording or sync authority. The library API can persist explicit immutable scopes and record all tracked files when every scope is private. The scope and commit commands below use that API, including rereading files edited after add.

title: CLI reference
section: Select scopes and record private files
text: Run scope and commit from the registered root or a descendant. Both require --repository PATH and --checkout ID exactly once, plus a complete matching locator. Use vcs open first to publish or recover that locator. Neither command infers a repository, checkout or scope. The configuration, marker and identity checks described for open also apply.

title: CLI reference
text: /path/to/gos v scope --repository /absolute/history.gossil --checkout work --scope private --path notes/plan.md --path notes/review.md --scope shared|private is required exactly once. Supply at least one --path PATH; repeat that option for each exact tracked path relative to the registered root. The one chosen scope applies to every path in this request. Paths must already be tracked. Duplicate paths, conflicting choices and unsupported path spellings fail without persisting a partial batch. The choice is immutable. Repeating the same choice is a checked no-op; changing it is refused. New choices advance the pending version once. A checkout can reopen with some scopes unselected or with both shared and private choices. Those states grant no recording or synchronization authority. Choosing shared scope prevents private recording of the complete tracked set. Shared recording and changing a persisted scope are not supported. Success prints Selected scopes: N followed by a newline. N is the number of requested paths, including choices already stored unchanged.

title: CLI reference
text: /path/to/gos v commit --repository /absolute/history.gossil --checkout work --scope private --all-tracked --user alice --comment 'Save notes' --date-override '2026-11-21T12:00:00' Required option Meaning --scope private Explicit request for owner-local private recording --all-tracked Include the complete tracked set; no path subset is accepted --user ACTOR Explicit nonempty actor text, at most 4096 UTF-8 bytes --comment TEXT Explicit nonempty comment, at most 1048576 UTF-8 bytes --date-override DATE Explicit native date text, at most 64 UTF-8 bytes Commit requires a nonempty tracked set with a stored private scope for every path. An unselected, shared or mixed set is refused before mutation. The command reads the complete tracked inventory and current checkout view; the library checks all seven view fields and reauthenticates owner, root, provider and scope. No caller-supplied replacement authority is accepted. Every commit rereads current bytes and executable modes. An edit needs no second add. Saving a file alone creates no history. Mode-only changes count as changes; mtime-only changes do not. Working files remain unchanged. The first private check-in names the empty shared root as its parent; later check-ins name both the previous private check-in and that shared root. The shared head stays unchanged. Dates must satisfy the native date grammar and be strictly later than every parent under native SQL date conversion. Actor, comment and date text must be UTF-8 without NUL. Comments containing [ are refused, including on a no-change request. This restriction narrows Fossil’s comment grammar. The command prints one of these lines, followed by a newline: Recorded private check-in: HASH No changes HASH is the new native check-in hash. An unchanged tree returns No changes without a new receipt or any changed head, counter, content or classification. A later add creates unselected paths again; select their private scope before recording the expanded tree.

title: CLI reference
text: Both commands accept separate option values only. They reject positional arguments, unknown or duplicate options, --name=value, --help, --root and --json. Only --path may repeat, and only for scope selection. Commit accepts no --path; scope accepts no recording metadata or --all-tracked. Both executable names and both group names use the same grammar. Checkout IDs are nonempty UTF-8, bounded to 1024 bytes. Scope selection and recording use the tracking limits above. These allow 4096 paths, 4096 bytes per path, 128 components, 64 MiB of retained working bytes and a 64 KiB read buffer. The temporary final file recheck can require another captured copy. Native content and parser limits also bound cumulative work across the complete operation. The library contract defines those budgets, immutable history checks, protected files and rollback guarantees. A capture, validation or transaction failure leaves no partial recording. An output failure returns status 1 and can occur after a durable scope change or private commit. A failed exit does not prove rollback. Reopen the same explicit binding and retry with unchanged files, valid metadata and a date later than the stored parents. After a durable commit, that retry prints No changes. Scope retries with the same choices preserve them unchanged.

title: CLI reference
text: The gos executable runs the same implementation as gossil. Both accept v as a short name for vcs. For example, this runs the same round-trip check: cargo run --locked --bin gos -- v test-delta FILE1 FILE2 Use either executable with either group name for initialization, native open, add/status, scope/commit, info, timeline/log, the three delta diagnostics and the prepared glob diagnostic. Usage messages use fixed spellings regardless of the invocation alias. Add and status use gos v; the other command usage messages use gossil vcs.

title: CLI reference
text: Success returns status 0. Usage, input, delta and output failures return status 1 with one diagnostic line on stderr. Missing input reports no such file: PATH. An output-open failure reports unable to open file "PATH" for writing. Invalid delta application reports Delta application failed.. A failed round trip reports delta test failed. Create and apply read their inputs before opening the output. This permits an output path to name an input file. Input or validation failures preserve an existing output, but an output write failure can leave it truncated. Parent folders must already exist. The encoder guide and decoder guide describe format bounds and the library errors behind these diagnostics. The getting started example uses distinct output files.

title: CLI reference
text: gossil-conformance is a separate development executable. It runs one explicit inherited-test configuration through just conformance CONFIG. It does not implement a Gossil engine. Its configuration, prerequisites and acceptance rules are in the runner guide.

title: CLI reference
text: Run info from the registered root or a descendant with a complete checkout locator: /path/to/gossil vcs info --repository /absolute/history.gossil --checkout work /path/to/gos v info --repository /absolute/history.gossil --checkout work Both executable names accept both vcs and v. Repository and checkout selections are required exactly once. The command accepts no revision argument, hash prefix, tag, --root or --json. Standalone --help or -h succeeds without reading a checkout. Success prints exactly five lines in this order: repository: "/absolute/history.gossil" local-root: "/absolute/work" checkout: FULL_CURRENT_NATIVE_ID shared-head: FULL_SHARED_NATIVE_ID private-head: FULL_PRIVATE_NATIVE_ID_OR_none Each line has one ASCII space after the colon and ends with LF, including the last line. Both paths are standard JSON strings with escaping for special characters. repository preserves the supplied UTF-8 spelling, including relative paths and symlink aliases, after successful admission. Non-UTF-8 repository input is rejected without lossy conversion. local-root is the authenticated canonical registered root. All heads are complete native IDs. checkout is the private combined head when present, otherwise the shared head. Before the first private recording, private-head is the literal none. The shared head stays at the initial public check-in after private recordings. Uncommitted edits do not change these recorded identities. Info authenticates the existing checkout before producing stdout. Wrong selections, missing or incomplete nearest locators, configuration conflicts and corrupted native state fail through the existing admission checks. Errors retain their underlying causes. Success and failure preserve repository logical state, locator bytes and working files. Database file bytes can change during provider admission. An output failure returns status 1 and can leave partial stdout. This command adapts Fossil’s current-tree checkout identity assertion from test/set-manifest.test:68-73 and the current-checkout branch of src/info.c. Fossil prints a 40-character checkout prefix, and its same_uuid helper accepts matching prefixes. The inherited test is copyright 2016 D. Richard Hipp under the Simplified BSD License. Gossil controls compare complete output IDs against an independently authenticated checkout view. This bounded subset does not implement Fossil’s full info interface, general timeline filters, parent traversal or historical revision selection. Unrelated inherited suites are outside this qualification.

title: CLI reference
text: Broader version-control commands and Gest task commands are planned. They are not accepted by gossil or gos. The short names above apply to initialization and the three delta diagnostics, the prepared glob diagnostic, native open, add/status, scope/commit, info and timeline/log. Shared recording, changing scopes, removal, rename, materialization, sync and Gest record associations remain unsupported.

title: CLI reference
text: Run from the registered checkout root or a descendant after vcs open has published a complete matching locator: just gossil vcs timeline --repository REPO --checkout ID just gossil v log --checkout ID --repository REPO Replace REPO and ID with the existing database and exact checkout identity. Both selectors are required, each once, with separate values in either order. Repository text is bounded to 4096 UTF-8 bytes and checkout text to 1024 bytes. Empty values, NUL, invalid UTF-8, duplicate or unknown options, positional arguments and --name=value forms fail. There are no filters, revision selectors, --limit or --json options. Output is always complete newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON), with one object per line. The eight forms are gossil vcs timeline, gossil vcs log, gossil v timeline, gossil v log, gos vcs timeline, gos vcs log, gos v timeline and gos v log. They emit identical bytes for the same admitted history. Standalone --help or -h after either command prints usage and exits 0 without opening storage. Help combined with selectors fails. Each compact JSON object has the keys hash, date, actor, comment and private, in exactly that order. The first four values are strings; private is a boolean. Every object ends with one LF, with no optional whitespace. Hashes are full native identities. Strict UTF-8 conversion and standard JSON escaping preserve the exact native date and decoded actor and comment, without normalization or date reformatting. The current check-in comes first and the immutable shared root occurs exactly once, last. Only the root has private: false. Before private recording, the root is the sole row. Opening uses existing-locator admission and publishes or repairs no locator. The API then authenticates the complete supported history in its own transaction. Neither operation reads working-file contents. Pending additions and dirty or deleted working files do not change the recorded output. Missing checkout, corrupt or unsupported state and exhausted bounds fail without a partial history. Opening admission, the API operation and serialization each have a separate finite allowance. They do not form one aggregate budget for the whole invocation. For serialization, N counts the UTF-8 source bytes of all four string values, including each hash once. The checked worst-case bound adds 6*N to the exact syntax overhead. That overhead is 61 bytes per private row or 62 per root row and includes keys, quotes, punctuation, boolean and LF. The cumulative bound must fit the CLI decoded-content limit and the platform allocation limit. The adapter reserves space once before serializing the complete response. The API records its result and completes its checked transaction before the adapter prepares output. Stdout receives no bytes until complete preflight and serialization succeed. Success exits 0. Failures exit 1 with a diagnostic and retain the original cause. A stdout write failure can leave partial stdout. The read preserves logical database state and working files; this contract makes no claim that physical database bytes remain identical. See qualification before treating this source command as released or installed. General Fossil timeline behavior and cat remain separate work.

title: CLI reference
text: The source accepts all four forms: gossil vcs test-glob PATTERN STRING ... gossil v test-glob PATTERN STRING ... gos vcs test-glob PATTERN STRING ... gos v test-glob PATTERN STRING ... Supply one pattern-list argument and at least one candidate argument. Arguments are positional; there are no switches, settings lookup or JSON mode. A token such as --help is a literal pattern or candidate when arity is valid. A pattern list beginning with @ fails with test-glob setting lookup is not implemented. Missing arguments fail with Usage: gossil vcs test-glob PATTERN STRING ... for every alias. For PATTERN equal to *.rs,src/* and candidates src/lib.rs and notes.md, the source-defined output is: SQL expression: (x GLOB '*.rs' OR x GLOB 'src/*') pattern[0] = [*.rs] pattern[1] = [src/*] 1 1 src/lib.rs 0 0 notes.md Pattern labels start at zero. Match indices start at one; zero means no match. Each candidate row prints reusable then one-shot results, followed by the original candidate bytes and LF. Pattern and candidate bytes are not escaped. The diagnostic constructs SQL with trusted expression x but executes no SQL. The adapter caps list and candidate inputs at 1 MiB each, pattern count at 65,536 and SQL output at 16 MiB. These bounds do not limit engine matching time or stack use. Unix arguments preserve raw bytes. Other platforms accept Unicode as UTF-8 and reject unrepresentable arguments with test-glob argument is not valid Unicode. Success exits 0. Usage, settings, encoding, budget, allocation and stdout errors exit 1. Budget messages use glob NAME limit exceeded; capacity overflow uses glob capacity overflow. Allocation messages begin glob allocation:. Stdout failures print unable to open file " " for writing, preserve the original I/O cause and may leave partial stdout. The command reads no repository, settings or files and changes no tracking state. The glob guide defines quotes, first-NUL truncation and the SQL parser’s extra advance after closing quotes. Historical controls used 0.9.30. The 2026-11-21 focused checkpoint exercised all four forms with 0.10.0; complete frozen-tree and delivery qualification are separate. These source forms make no claim about installed previews.

title: CLI reference
text: Use the three diagnostics for file deltas. For a native checkout, initialize a new repository, then register one explicit existing root with open. Next, reopen without --root, add explicit files, select private scope and commit all tracked paths. Use info to inspect the recorded checkout identity. Follow the source walkthrough and preserve durable state when a command reports an output failure.

title: Compare Gossil with Git
text: Gossil is designed to keep agent files, typed issues and their connections to code in one coordinated history alongside Git. A historical view selects an exact file head, complete issue and discussion boundaries, and versioned links between issues and code. Git remains the source-code authority. This page compares that intended design with Git’s available behavior. The source CLI initializes empty repositories without a checkout, registers or reopens one native checkout and offers three delta diagnostics. It also supports explicit add and status without recording file content. Status distinguishes pending and recorded paths and shows their actual scope. The Rust library has typed task, project and author converters, a task artifact emitter, and native storage primitives. It does not yet create or read persisted issues. Native checkout open registers or reopens an existing directory and publishes its lookup locator. The library can record the complete private tracked tree. The source scope and commit commands expose that operation with explicit selections and metadata. Issue commands remain planned. See the current limits and CLI reference before trying a command.

title: Compare Gossil with Git
text: In Git, the working tree contains the files you edit. The index is the staging area for the next commit. Normally, a commit records the index as a file tree, with parents and a message. You can stage selected changes before committing; a commit need not include every edit on disk. See the Git tutorial and commit reference. Git can version task documents, plans and evidence in that same tree. Branches and commit history support many ways to organize the work. Git notes can attach information to an object without changing that object; notes have their own references and history. See Git notes. Need Git Intended Gossil design Record selected files Commits retain trees selected through the index or commit options Native file check-ins retain explicitly tracked agent files Record a task Version a task document or use a chosen tracker and integration Typed project/task records have defined fields, identities and reconstruction rules Select an earlier review state Name commits and any separately required task or notes history Select the file head plus complete exact boundaries for issues, links and discussions Connect an issue to code Adopt conventions or tools for references and reverse lookup Version typed links to registered Git repositories and support lookup in both directions Coordinate related changes A commit can include code and task documents in one tree One local database transaction coordinates selected Gossil files, records, scope and checkout heads Keep private agent material Choose a repository layout and sharing policy Keep private and shared material within one repository, with an explicit internal boundary A standalone tracker beside Git or Fossil can also retain detailed history. The extra requirement is to coordinate the exact states and dependencies that belong to a review. Gossil defines that coordination as part of its repository model, rather than leaving it to a convention between independent tools. Fossil already has immutable ticket artifacts and file history. The repository guide explains Gossil’s specified additions.

title: Compare Gossil with Git
text: Suppose an agent revises plan.md, marks its task ready for review, and saves a private trace of a failed approach. The implementation is in a separate Git repository. In the planned Gossil workflow: Review the plan diff, task changes and permitted evidence together. Request the integrated operation with the expected file and issue revisions. Record the Gossil artifacts, derived records, scope, local command history and checkout heads in one database transaction. Retain the permitted file head and the complete issue boundaries for later review. A file head identifies a file check-in. An issue boundary identifies its scope, complete contributing artifact set and projection version. Artifacts are immutable stored records; the projection version names the rules that reconstruct the issue’s values. Contributors include losing assignments even when a current screen displays other values. Notes, links and discussions need their required dependencies too. If the agent later changes only the task’s status, the file head stays the same. The earlier issue boundary still selects the state reviewed with the plan. Record-only changes create no file check-in. Later arrivals do not silently change that selected historical set, subject to permission and byte availability. A file hash alone cannot recover this context. The code link names a registered Git repository, full commit, path and blob, with a versioned selector when it names a range. The blob identifies file bytes. From the issue, a reviewer can reach the pinned code; from that code version, the reviewer can find the issue. A known filename or current checkout path helps locate material, but neither supplies its repository identity or historical version. Local paths can change without changing the registered repository’s identity. The design introduces no global file identity. Uncommitted code needs a captured snapshot. An authorized capture can retain bytes if the external Git checkout later disappears; an object reference alone does not guarantee availability. The link descriptor encoding remains unfinished. See the repository guide for the planned coordination and its limits. The integrated transaction commits changes to the Gossil database. An external Git commit remains a separate operation. Checkout files are written after database commit through recoverable work, so filesystem recovery can still be necessary. Ordinary issue edits do not automatically batch unrelated work.

title: Compare Gossil with Git
text: The planned Gossil checkout root can sit above several Git repositories. Select AGENTS.md and chosen agent files inside those repositories explicitly; initialization does not track every descendant. Gossil’s selection is independent of the nested Git indices and must preserve their branches and commits. The repository guide shows how to choose this layout. Git ignore rules help omit untracked files; they do not affect files already tracked. Sparse checkout controls which tracked paths appear in the working tree. Neither mechanism establishes a private/shared boundary for stored history. See gitignore and sparse checkout. Git transfer can select references through refspecs, which map source references to destinations. This selects history to fetch, not a confidentiality policy for individual paths. Access rules depend on the chosen repository and service configuration. See Git fetch. Gossil’s chosen design keeps private and shared history in one local repository. Shared history must be usable without private-only dependencies. Team replication, sync and autosync remain planned; this design does not promise arbitrary partial sharing within the shared portion today. This page follows the nossaifd writing guide, including principles credited to Rosalind Reid, Shreya Shankar and Oskar Austegard.

title: Compare Gossil with Git
text: The private recorder saves a snapshot of every tracked file. Add enrolls paths rather than staging their bytes. The recorder reads those paths again, so it includes edits made without re-adding. Each path needs an explicit immutable private scope choice before recording. This operation creates owner-local file history and leaves the shared empty root unchanged. Shared recording and synchronization remain unsupported. The qualification record separates the checked library checkpoint from the CLI checkpoint still awaiting final gates. The installed tracking release, version 0.5.0, includes neither scope selection nor private recording. The source library also reads complete recorded ancestry through recorded_timeline. Its rows preserve full native hashes and exact metadata bytes, current first and shared root last. The source timeline and log commands print those rows as compact NDJSON with explicit selectors and an existing matching locator. This bounded reader does not establish general Fossil timeline compatibility.

title: Compare Gossil with Git
text: The glob source matches bounded Fossil pattern lists and constructs SQL expressions. It adds no ignore rules, filesystem traversal or wildcard selection to add or status. Its focused source checkpoint passed with the selected 0.10.0 engine. Complete frozen-tree and delivery qualification are separate.

title: Compare Gossil with Git
text: Keep Git for source work today. Next, try the delta tutorial and use the repository guide to select agent files. For a future integrated review, retain the exact file head, complete issue boundaries and versioned code links together.

title: Library concepts
text: Gossil separates byte operations, artifact structure and local database ownership. A byte operation does not create a repository, and a parsed artifact does not establish its place in a repository graph. For file selection, check-ins, branches and sharing, read working with repositories. This page describes the library modules available to application authors.

title: Library concepts
section: Files and issues in one operation
text: The intended product coordinates agent files and structured issue records in one repository database. A local operation can commit a plan revision, its task change and a private trace together. Its transaction includes canonical artifacts, derived projections, scope, local command history and Gossil checkout heads. A projection is stored state reconstructed from retained artifact records. Git remains the external source authority; its commits are separate operations. Checkout filesystem writes follow database commit through recoverable work. This integrated workflow remains planned. A historical view selects a permitted file check-in and exact record boundaries for each issue or discussion. The record boundary names the complete contributor set and projection version, with all dependencies required by the claimed view. Contributors are immutable artifacts that determine the record’s state. The projection version identifies the reconstruction rules; scope distinguishes shared access from an authorized owner’s combined view. Record-only changes create no file check-in, so a file hash alone cannot identify issue history. Later arrivals do not change the selected historical set. Access still depends on permission and byte availability. Typed links connect an issue to exact code versions and support reverse lookup from code to issues. A Git target pins its registered repository, commit, path and blob, with a versioned selector for a range. Captures can retain the permitted bytes; an object ID alone does not guarantee their availability. Shared history must be complete without private-only dependencies. Receiving it does not automatically update a checkout or an owner’s private issue selection. Explicit update and publication enforce the relevant revision and scope checks. A descriptor is a structured record naming a versioned link target and any selected range. Its transferable encoding remains unfinished, so these guides do not yet give a format that applications can exchange. Fossil supplies immutable file and ticket history; Gest supplies task workflows. Gossil’s specified additions coordinate exact issue boundaries with shared/private file heads and strengthen Gest’s multi-statement helpers with one owned transaction. Planned command undo validates complete inverse changes and rejects stale dependencies; it retains artifacts and does not rewind Git. Read compare Gossil with Git for the plan/task example and working with repositories for file selection. The library modules below form the implemented subset.

title: Library concepts
text: The delta module creates and applies Fossil deltas. Application takes an explicit output limit. The compression module packs and unpacks blobs, which are stored byte sequences. Unpacking also takes a decoded size limit. The content_hash module computes content digests. A digest identifies bytes but does not grant access to them. The artifact_checksum module computes legacy MD5 checksums for artifact records. It does not choose the repository’s content hash policy.

title: Library concepts
text: The token_codec module escapes byte values for Fossil record tokens. Its byte and C-string forms have different zero-byte behavior. The token guide defines those contracts. The artifact module parses eight structural artifact types with explicit limits and checks their structure and checksums. A caller implements DateProvider, whose julianday method converts date fields to Julian day numbers. Repository graph validation requires more storage rules. See the parser guide.

title: Library concepts
text: LocalStore owns a local libSQL connection and one exclusive write transaction. A transaction must commit or roll back before the connection returns to the store. The public interface does not expose arbitrary SQL. LocalOwnerRepository initializes a complete empty public root. Its initialize constructor creates a repository without a checkout. The vcs init command calls this constructor, generates identities and a password, and selects a default administrator from the environment. The API requires those values explicitly. Its create constructor creates catalog1 and binds an existing checkout directory. Catalog1 and catalog4 name storage formats; the native storage guide defines their creation and admission rules. After initialize, register_checkout can register one existing directory in catalog4. checkout_view authenticates its ID; checkout_view_for_root authenticates its exact root. These library methods change no working files and publish no locator. The source vcs open adapter adds locator publication and recovery around those admitted database operations. Open does not select additional files. Generic private content writes require the bound catalog1 repository and refuse catalog4. Catalog4 has a separate private recording API, described below. Its shared root stays a check-in with no files. Admission validates the stored root and authority before repository operations. For catalog4, it also validates the complete supported tracking, scope and private history state. SharedView restricts access to public content that passed this validation. Read and write access to the database file through the operating system establishes local owner authority. The native storage guide defines admission, content bounds and access rules. General links between artifacts in the repository graph remain planned, so parsing does not establish parent relationships or resolve references. Sync and team authentication also remain planned.

title: Library concepts
text: Gest is a task and artifact tracker. These converters use its task, project and author record model. The gest_task_values module validates eleven already decoded task fields. It returns an owned record with a standardized status and UTC timestamps. The task values guide defines validation and caller responsibilities. The gest_project_values module validates the four fields that make up the canonical Gest project record, gest_id, archived_at, created_at and updated_at. It returns an owned record with an identifier, nullable archive time and UTC timestamps. The project values guide defines the complete field contract. A local checkout root is outside the canonical project record. The gest_author_values module validates six canonical author fields and returns an owned record. It preserves names and nullable email exactly, normalizes author types and converts timestamps to UTC. The author values guide defines this conversion separately from native actors and local principals. The task ticket emitter produces bounded creation artifact bytes from a validated task, a separate native ticket identity, actor bytes and a typed UTC date. Before passing decoded task, project or author values to a converter, callers must check raw field presence, duplicates and byte limits. Storage integration and task, project or author commands remain separate work.

title: Library concepts
text: Tracking and scope are separate choices. add_files enrolls paths without staging their bytes. An absent scope row means unselected, not shared or private. select_path_scopes persists an immutable PathScope::Shared or PathScope::Private choice for an already tracked path. Repeating an equal choice is a checked no-op; changing a choice is unsupported. commit_private_tracked_files requires every tracked path to have private scope. The caller supplies the complete path set and the latest CheckoutView. The recorder captures current bytes and executable modes, so edits after add need no second add. It writes one complete private check-in and updates the combined head while leaving the empty shared head unchanged. The combined head selects the owner’s private tree together with the shared tree, which is empty in this supported recording family. The operation validates the full supported history and its derived rows. A content budget bounds stored, decoded and retained bytes. A parser ledger counts input bytes, cards, owned bytes and entries across parsed artifacts. Both bound work across admission, capture, construction and final validation. An unchanged tree returns NoChange without a new receipt or changed head or counter. Working files remain unchanged. Read native storage for request metadata and limits. Shared recording, synchronization and integrated issue operations remain planned. The source scope and commit commands use these library contracts. They require the complete locator binding and explicit repository, checkout and scope selections. Commit also requires all-tracked consent and explicit actor, comment and date. Final CLI qualification is still pending. The library reader recorded_timeline returns the complete current-first ancestry through the shared empty root. It authenticates all native history before reading original metadata in the same transaction. It reads no working-file contents and returns no partial result when a bound fails. See the recorded ancestry contract. The source timeline and log commands print those rows as compact NDJSON after existing-locator admission and checked API completion. Opening, the API and serialization have separate finite bounds.

title: Library concepts
text: The prepared glob module parses Fossil pattern lists and calls the selected libSQL engine for matching. A result is the first matching one-based pattern index, or zero. Its finite limits bound bytes and pattern counts, not engine matching time or stack use. Matching selects no files and traverses no directories. glob_expr builds SQL from a trusted expression and escaped patterns. Bind untrusted candidate values through SQL parameters in a caller-owned connection; never put those bytes in the expression argument. The storage API still exposes no arbitrary SQL. The glob guide describes the distinct SQL parser advance and the current qualification limits.

title: Library concepts
text: Choose the smallest module that fits the operation. Next, set resource limits at every decoding or parsing boundary and read that module’s error contract.

title: Inherited-test runner
text: gossil-conformance executes one Fossil Tcl suite against an explicit program. It is development infrastructure and implements no Gossil engine behavior. A reference run tests the pinned upstream Fossil program. A candidate run tests the replacement program whose compatibility is under development. The runs have separate configurations and output directories. A missing candidate never falls back to C Fossil. Run just conformance-self-test to check the runner controls. These tests pass when the runner correctly rejects deliberate failures and incomplete runs. That result does not mean the inherited Fossil suites pass.

title: Inherited-test runner
text: Install Rust with Cargo, Git, Just and uv on PATH before using the recipes. Rust builds the runner, Just runs Justfile recipes, and uv runs the installed workflow tools. just setup supplies the Linux reference tools and fetches Cargo dependencies. just install --check checks the saved workflow installation. The required references are Tcl 8.6.18 and Fossil 2.29 at revision 7e8ecf0ce4, with TLS and FUSE disabled. On Linux, just setup builds these tools from the archives pinned in evidence/reference-tools.json. It needs a C compiler, Make, zlib development headers and CA certificates. The Tcl installation retains its shell, shared library and core runtime scripts. Verified tools become available through ignored .jlog/bin links after the complete installation is published. Its receipt retains source identities, configure flags and binary hashes. Repeated setup checks and reuses that installation. Changed cache bytes and unknown tool paths fail without replacement. Worktrees can check and reuse shared managed references read-only when their source receipt, binary hashes and runtime observations match. On other hosts, setup checks and keeps the existing reference tools. Supply them before setup if they are absent. The current macOS tools remain the existing Tcl installation in Homebrew storage and the pinned local Fossil build. Setup does not adopt those external tools into its managed Linux installation. The read-only pull-request release check runs just setup before the full just check. Only a successful push to main can run its source-tag job. Local Linux native-tool controls and Python installer controls are separate from Rust coverage and the full Rust suite in CI. The bounded native setup receipt records the executed Linux scope.

title: Inherited-test runner
text: Write a JSON configuration with absolute paths. The following example uses the checked-in positive control. Replace /path/to/gossil with the checkout path. The output directory must not exist. Save this example as CONFIG.json. { "role": "reference", "revision": "b3a1c8efb2731dffbd5cc38c58ac349746de6da6", "tcl": "/path/to/gossil/.jlog/bin/tclsh", "driver": "/path/to/gossil/tests/fixtures/controls/tester.tcl", "executable": "/path/to/gossil/.jlog/bin/fossil", "suite": "pass", "run_dir": "/path/to/gossil/target/conformance/example", "timeout_ms": 3000, "seed": 20261117, "inputs": [ "/path/to/gossil/tests/fixtures/fossil/tester.tcl", "/path/to/gossil/tests/fixtures/fossil/enable.patch" ], "capabilities": {"tls": "disabled", "fuse": "disabled"} }

title: Inherited-test runner
text: Field Meaning and effect role Required label reference or candidate. It does not select a binary. revision Nonempty source identifier retained in evidence. The runner does not verify a source checkout against it. tcl Absolute path to an executable Tcl interpreter. driver Absolute path to the enabled tester.tcl driver. executable Absolute path to the program under test, used without fallback. suite Suite basename without a slash, for example pass for pass.test. run_dir Absolute path to a new output directory whose parent already exists. timeout_ms Positive deadline in milliseconds. A timeout rejects the run. seed Unsigned 32-bit value passed to Tcl srand before the driver runs. It controls Tcl randomness, not every source of randomness in the tested program. inputs Absolute paths to extra source, fixture or patch files whose bytes need hashing. capabilities Caller-supplied string map retained as evidence. It neither enables features nor verifies their availability. invocation_plan Optional complete plan and corpus pins; omitted or null uses strict duplicate-name rejection. See the plan contract below. The runner locates  .test beside driver. The example runs tests/fixtures/controls/pass.test. For an upstream suite, keep the original source tree and corpus unchanged. Put a copy of tester.tcl and the selected suite beside each other in a separate harness directory. Apply tests/fixtures/fossil/enable.patch only to the copied driver. Prepend set argv0 /absolute/path/to/original/test/tester.tcl to that enabled copy, using the original driver path in the pinned source tree. This restores the original corpus location when the driver derives testdir from argv0. Set driver to the enabled copy. The executed delta1 harness uses this layout; its original driver, suite and corpus bytes remain unchanged. The runner hashes the driver, suite, interpreter and tested executable automatically, in addition to every path in inputs. The example’s revision is the Git mirror commit for the inherited source. Fossil identifies the same source snapshot with its native revision, starting 7e8ecf0ce4. The full pair and driver hashes are in the repository file evidence/baselines/fossil/provenance.json. The label alone does not prove that an executable was built from that source. Create the parent output folder, then run just conformance CONFIG.json. Exit status 0 means this suite passed, status 1 means it failed acceptance, and status 2 means setup failed. The runner prints the report.json path. The report retains decoded stdout and stderr, commands, environment, hashes, source pin, suite, original assertion names, seed, capabilities and process status. The log files retain exact bytes and their hashes. Invalid UTF-8 blocks acceptance. Only stdout supplies assertion records, while stderr remains evidence. Without a plan, assertion identity combines the source pin, suite path and original name. The runner does not infer parameterized cases or unreported seeds. Callers must supply all fixture and source inputs that need hashing. Framework checks remain separate from real assertions. Known-bug annotations remain visible, but an assertion reported as failing never becomes a pass. Skipped summaries produce not-run with the original reason. The runner has no automatic feature-disabled mapping. A separate analysis must link the skipped reason to a capability observation, as the reference archive described in evidence/baselines/README.md does. The configuration map alone does not establish that classification. Timeouts and incomplete output produce blocked. Only pass contributes to acceptance. A skip or blocked result prevents acceptance of the entire suite, even if other assertions pass. A framework-only run fails acceptance. The runner also rejects missing summaries, inconsistent counts and crashes. For example, the final summary for one passing assertion is ***** Final results: 0 errors out of 1 tests. A final summary invalidates the run if a count is nonnumeric or exceeds the range of usize, Rust’s unsigned pointer-sized integer type. Every final-summary occurrence counts, including malformed ones. A duplicate summary or a later valid summary cannot clear that rejection.

title: Inherited-test runner
text: The default parser rejects repeated original assertion names. Some inherited suites reuse names for different source files. Such a run can opt into a complete, ordered plan of expected source-derived invocation identities. The plan preserves every original name, result, annotation and framework flag. Add an invocation_plan object to the configuration: { "invocation_plan": { "path": "/absolute/path/invocation-plan.json", "sha256": "EXPECTED_PLAN_SHA256", "expected_invocations": 22804, "corpus_manifest": "/absolute/path/corpus-manifest.json", "corpus_manifest_sha256": "EXPECTED_MANIFEST_SHA256", "corpus_root": "/absolute/path/upstream" } } expected_invocations pins the complete row count and must be positive. A count pin catches truncated plans during setup. It does not prove source correspondence. Both expected hashes must be lowercase SHA-256 values. The runner checks them before execution and parses those same verified bytes. The plan binds the configured suite, upstream revision, exact suite bytes and corpus manifest. The manifest binds every original corpus input. All physical paths are absolute. The runner assumes that no process changes input files during a run. This immutable-input assumption also applies to the existing input-hashing contract. Hash verification does not remove the race if another writer changes an input after verification. A plan uses schema gossil.invocation-plan.v1. Each row contains name and id. An ID contains suite and a structured position. Corpus positions use kind: "corpus", an upstream-relative source, a zero-based iteration and a positive slot. Empty controls use kind: "empty" with a positive index. The final framework position uses kind: "framework". For delta1, slot identifies one of the three assertions in each mutation iteration, numbered 1 through 3. The empty-control index identifies one of three final empty-input assertions, also numbered 1 through 3. The complete object shapes are shown below. These illustrative objects have one corpus row. They are not a complete plan for the real delta1 suite. Replace all hash placeholders with hashes of the exact bytes and include every real row. { "schema": "gossil.invocation-plan.v1", "suite": "delta1", "revision": "PINNED_REVISION", "suite_sha256": "SUITE_SHA256", "corpus_manifest_sha256": "MANIFEST_SHA256", "rows": [ {"name": "delta-example-0-1", "id": {"suite": "delta1", "position": { "kind": "corpus", "source": "test/example.txt", "iteration": 0, "slot": 1 }}} ] } The corresponding manifest has this shape: { "suite": "delta1", "revision": "PINNED_REVISION", "files": {"test/example.txt": "FILE_SHA256"} } Source paths use forward slashes and contain no empty, dot or parent components. IDs must be unique, and plan rows must cover every manifest source. Review of the generator and source establishes correspondence for every invocation. Hashes bind supplied bytes. text: API: apply gives the exact contract. gossil::delta applies Fossil deltas to byte slices. A delta describes output with literal bytes and copies from an original byte slice. title: Bounded delta decoder
text: From the repository root, run: cargo run --locked --bin gossil -- vcs test-delta-apply ORIGIN DELTA TARGET Replace ORIGIN, DELTA and TARGET with file paths. Quote paths that contain spaces. The command reads both inputs and finishes decoding before it opens TARGET. The target can be the same path as either input. On success, it writes exactly the decoded bytes, returns status 0 and leaves stdout and stderr empty. Cargo may print build messages on stderr before the executable runs. The command returns status 1 for usage, read, decode, allocation or write errors. The characterized diagnostics are: Failure Stderr line Unsupported command or argument count Usage: gossil vcs test-delta-apply ORIGIN DELTA TARGET Missing input no such file: PATH Delta rejection or buffer reservation failure Delta application failed. Target open or write failure unable to open file "PATH" for writing Each diagnostic ends with one LF byte, and stdout remains empty. Other input read errors include the path and the underlying I/O error. The command has no root-level test-delta-apply alias. Usage, input-read and decode failures preserve an existing target because it has not been opened. A write failure can leave a truncated or partially written target. The command does not replace files atomically.

title: Bounded delta decoder
text: The decoder API exposes output_size, apply, Limits and DeltaError. The same module also exposes the encoder function create. output_size(delta) parses only the advertised output size and its LF delimiter. It does not validate the commands or enforce the output limit used by apply. use gossil::delta::{Limits, apply, output_size}; let delta = b"3\n3:ABC0;"; assert_eq!(output_size(delta).unwrap(), 3); let output = apply(b"", delta, Limits { max_output_bytes: 1024 }).unwrap(); assert_eq!(output, b"ABC"); apply(source, delta, limits) returns Result , DeltaError>. The result has exactly the advertised size, with no trailing NUL byte. Both input slices must fit within i32::MAX bytes. The output ceiling is the smaller of limits.max_output_bytes and i32::MAX. Limits::default() uses i32::MAX, as does the file diagnostic. The first pass checks command syntax, source ranges, literal lengths, cumulative output length and the final size. After validation, the decoder reserves output storage with a fallible operation and replays the checked slices in a second pass. It stores no list of parsed operations. Invalid commands reach no output reservation. An empty result needs no reservation. The decoder returns these DeltaError variants: Error variant Meaning MissingHeaderNewline Header digits are not followed by LF. InputTooLarge A source or delta input exceeds the signed-length envelope. OutputTooLarge The advertised output exceeds the effective ceiling. TruncatedCommand A numeric command has no following operator. MissingCopyComma A copy offset has no present comma delimiter. UnknownOperator An operator byte is not defined. SourceRange A copy exceeds the source, including a zero copy beyond its end. OutputRange A command would exceed the advertised output. TruncatedLiteral A literal has fewer bytes than its count. Unterminated The input ends or reaches a command-start NUL before a semicolon. SizeMismatch A semicolon arrives before the advertised output is complete. AllocationFailed Output reservation failed, with the original TryReserveError retained as its cause. Fallible reservation reports recoverable allocation failures. It does not guarantee recovery from an operating-system kill or memory exhaustion after a successful reservation.

title: Bounded delta decoder
text: A delta starts with the encoded output length and LF. The form COUNT:BYTES inserts a literal, COUNT@OFFSET, copies from the source, and CHECKSUM; ends the delta. All numbers use the alphabet below. The decoder uses the exact unsigned-byte digit alphabet: 0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ_abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz~ Numbers wrap modulo 2^32, and empty numeric fields mean zero. High-bit bytes are not aliases for ASCII digits or delimiters. Zero-count copies still require a valid source offset and a comma. Literal payloads can contain arbitrary bytes. The decoder requires a semicolon and an exact final output size, then ignores trailing bytes. Checksum verification is disabled, as it is in the pinned reference build. The numeric field before the semicolon is parsed but not checked against the output. Accepted wrong-checksum fixtures remain accepted. Checked ranges and slice access reject truncation at boundaries where the C implementation can read beyond its logical input. Those C pointer behaviors are not format guarantees.

title: Bounded delta encoder
text: The encoder follows the pinned Fossil src/delta.c algorithm. It indexes source landmarks, scans target windows for matching source bytes, and emits copies when they cover their encoding overhead. Other bytes become literals. Its rolling hash uses sixteen signed bytes, matching the selected native build. Checksums sum unsigned big-endian four-byte words with wrapping arithmetic and right-zero padding for the last short word. Sources of at most sixteen bytes produce one literal, including a zero-length literal for an empty target. Longer sources omit that zero literal. The hash tables omit the last complete source block and visit newer landmarks first. Each target window examines at most 250 candidates. Backward extension stops before source offset zero. A match equal to its encoding overhead is accepted. Equal-length candidates retain the first visited match, and the first target window with a winning match emits it immediately. Both inputs must fit within i32::MAX bytes. The encoder counts integer digits with unsigned arithmetic. The native signed shift above 2^30 is undefined. Unsigned counting there is a safe Rust policy and does not promise giant-input native parity. Slice lengths and addresses remain bounded by existing inputs. Every output append reserves storage before extending the vector. Both hash tables also reserve before initialization. EncoderAllocationFailed records the buffer stage, requested element count and original TryReserveError cause. The source and target size checks reuse InputTooLarge. Tests exercise genuine capacity-overflow errors without asking the allocator for giant storage. Fallible reservation does not promise recovery from an operating-system kill.
