title: Local database ownership
text: API: LocalStore gives the exact contract. The storage module opens local libSQL files and owns one write transaction at a time. Its low-level lifecycle API also supports the validated native storage boundary. That boundary installs the complete schema and implements empty-root initialization, one native directory registration, explicit tracking and scopes, private file recording and bounded catalog1 content operations. The native storage guide defines the catalog formats. Opening that higher-level repository validates its stored root and authority metadata. Migration and broader adapters remain unimplemented. Both LocalOwnerRepository::create and LocalOwnerRepository::initialize refuse existing -journal, -wal and -shm entries beside the destination before creating the database. They preserve those entries, including dangling symlinks and directories. Observation failures retain the operating-system cause. The checks append literal native filename suffixes. They observe the namespace before creation and again before SQLite entry. Callers must keep that namespace stable through engine cleanup. The constructors observe regular-file identity at separate boundaries. These observations do not establish atomic binding to an engine handle. Checkout-free initialization retains a failed main file if the engine might have opened it or COMMIT was attempted. It reports cleanup uncertainty separately from the first operation error.

title: Local database ownership
text: use gossil::storage::{LocalStore, StorageError}; async fn lifecycle(path: &std::path::Path) -> Result  { let mut store = LocalStore::open(path).await?; store.begin_write().await?.commit().await?; store.begin_write().await?.rollback().await?; Ok(()) } The example opens the database and terminates empty transactions. Use LocalOwnerRepository for admitted native content operations. The example above uses only the low-level lifecycle API. LocalStore::open(path) builds a local database and retains one connection. It treats nonempty paths as literal native filenames, including relative names that begin with file: and names that contain ?, # or %. On Unix, it preserves filename bytes that are not valid UTF-8 when the filesystem accepts them. A filesystem rejection remains an open error. An embedded NUL returns an error with the original std::ffi::NulError cause. An empty path retains SQLite’s temporary-database behavior and fails the required WAL check. Every file open sets and reads back WAL, foreign keys ON, synchronous=FULL and a 5000 ms busy timeout. WAL is SQLite’s write-ahead journal mode. An open fails if configuration differs from these requirements. begin_write(&mut self) takes the connection before it issues BEGIN IMMEDIATE. The returned WriteTransaction, the transaction owner, exclusively borrows the store. A second owner cannot borrow it at the same time. There is no public SQL, connection, statement or lazy query interface. An internal execution error marks the owner rollback-only, which means later internal operations cannot issue SQL and commit must reject the operation. Queries materialize results by collecting rows into owned values before returning. They consume their statements and rows inside the owner. Preparation, stepping and value-decoding errors follow the same failure path. The native content operations also latch non-SQL failures through the owner. Fixture SQL uses the same private execution and row-collection code as the storage boundary. Explicit commit and rollback return the connection only after SQLite reports that no transaction remains active. A commit error triggers checked rollback when the transaction remains active. Errors retain the original engine cause and report a separate cleanup failure when one occurs. If commit fails but checked rollback restores an idle connection, the store can begin another write. The commit still returns its original error. commit_checked() returns a CommitFailure with the original operation error and an optional cleanup error. Both retain their typed source chains through StorageError::source() when an underlying cause exists. Inspect operation first and cleanup separately. commit() keeps its existing StorageError result and stores cleanup diagnostics as text. A failed BEGIN or cleanup discards the connection and poisons the store. A poisoned store requires an explicit new open.

title: Local database ownership
text: Dropping a WriteTransaction without explicit termination poisons the store and drops its sole connection. The destructor executes no SQL and polls no future. The pinned local libSQL connection uses SQLite’s close_v2 API. SQLite rolls back an active transaction when the connection is destroyed. This depends on the module keeping statements and other connection aliases inside the owner. Local SQL calls block their current asynchronous poll, including busy waits. The cancellation fixture aborts at a controlled await between SQL calls and awaits task destruction before checking writer progress. Cancellation after a successful COMMIT leaves committed rows in the database. It cannot undo a commit whose result the outer caller has not received. A later server adapter must define its blocking scheduling and result-delivery boundaries.

title: Local database ownership
text: LocalStore supplies transaction ownership. LocalOwnerRepository adds the repository, checkout and history checks required by the private recording library. Opening a LocalStore alone does not establish those prerequisites. The recorder validates the complete supported history, captures every explicitly private tracked file, and writes content, a manifest, its receipt and derived rows in one transaction. Helpers borrow the operation’s content budget and parser ledger throughout. Failure rolls back earlier database writes, and recording never writes the working files. The qualification record distinguishes the checked library checkpoint from the CLI awaiting final gates. It does not add public SQL access or change the lifecycle guarantees above.

title: Local database ownership
text: Use LocalStore to own a transaction, or LocalOwnerRepository for validated repository operations. Prefer commit_checked() when a caller needs to inspect both error causes. Next, consult the generated Rust API for the chosen type’s signatures and errors.

title: Native local storage
text: API: LocalOwnerRepository gives the exact contract. The storage API creates an empty native repository without a checkout. After registration, its catalog4 library can track paths, select explicit scopes and record the complete private tracked tree through one owned libSQL transaction. The shared history remains the initial empty check-in. General artifact crosslinks, Gest projections and filesystem recovery remain planned. Catalog names identify storage formats. Catalog1 binds a checkout at creation and supports bounded private content bytes. Catalog4 starts without a checkout and supports one later registration. Generic catalog1 content writes remain separate from catalog4 recording.

title: Native local storage
text: LocalOwnerRepository::initialize(path, InitializeOptions) creates a native repository without registering a checkout. Supply the project and local owner identities, administrator, password, SQLite date expression, SHA1 selection and finite content/parser limits. The API requires an explicit administrator. It does not read environment variables or a preference database. The vcs init CLI adapter supplies generated identities and a password, and chooses the administrator from options or the environment. It uses this strict catalog4 contract; it does not bind a checkout. Initialization normalizes the date for the root D card. It installs the native default report, system users and administrator password digest. SHA1 selection sets the native hash policy and hashes the actual root with SHA1. Otherwise the root uses SHA3-256. initialization_identity() returns the stored project-code and server-code after checking admission. This constructor installs catalog4 with checkout_count=0. Its only nonempty g_* tables are g_storage, g_local_owner and g_public_receipt. Reopen authenticates the single canonical empty root, its native hash, date, event, branch tags and receive/index facts. It checks the exact schema, complete policy, owner binding and foreign keys. The remaining local tables must be empty, except for the exact registration, tracking, scope and private recording inventories described below. Extra native content or indexed history outside that family refuses admission. Persisted issue projections and states mixing those issues with file history remain unsupported. Catalog5 and catalog6 also remain unsupported. No upgrade occurs on open. Generic private content writes through this handle refuse catalog4. The destination and its recovery neighbors must remain stable through engine cleanup. Existing destinations and recovery entries are preserved. Failures retain the first cause and report cleanup uncertainty separately. A possibly opened engine or an attempted commit prevents automatic main-file removal. Pathname observations do not certify engine disposal or atomic binding. Templates, global preferences and project display fields are outside this API.

title: Native local storage
text: After checkout-free initialization, call LocalOwnerRepository::register_checkout(checkout_id, root, limits) to register one existing directory against the initial empty root. This API supports only catalog4 with no existing registration. It refuses catalog1 and a second registration, including a retry with the same ID or an alias of the same root. Supply a nonempty, NUL-free checkout ID of at most 1024 UTF-8 bytes. Supply an existing directory with a nonempty, NUL-free UTF-8 path of at most 4096 bytes, both before and after canonicalization. Both ceilings also use the smaller limits.parser.input_bytes. Relative paths and caller aliases resolve to the canonical directory. Persisted roots must retain their exact canonical spelling, device, inode and owner binding on every admission. Canonical components are observed without following links. Callers must keep the namespace stable. These pathname observations do not protect against hostile concurrent replacement. Registration uses one exclusive database transaction. It checks the saved admission proof and complete native state before writing one checkout row, one owner row and checkout_count=1. It writes exactly the three native keys checkout, checkout-hash and fingerprint. These keys retain the actual initial root RID, its hash and the native fingerprint derived from the receive record. The API validates the complete result and captures its proof before checked commit. It replaces the saved proof only after known success. Earlier writes roll back on failure. The lifecycle rules still govern commit and cleanup uncertainty. The returned CheckoutView owns the repository ID, checkout ID, canonical root, shared head, combined head, generation and pending version. The combined head selects the owner’s private tree together with the shared tree, which is empty in this recording family. At registration, the shared head is the public initial root, the combined head is absent, and both counters are zero. A later private recording advances the combined head while the shared head stays fixed. checkout_view(checkout_id, limits) authenticates that exact persisted registration. checkout_view_for_root(root, limits) authenticates the sole registration for the explicitly chosen canonical root. Both methods revalidate complete native state and refuse stale authority, invalid bindings or unsupported inventory. Root lookup refuses absence, another root, unauthorized ownership and multiple registrations. It allocates no identity and repairs no registration or native key. Ordinary files and nested Git repositories in the directory remain unselected and unchanged. Registration creates no file check-in, materializes no files and publishes no ROOT/.gossil/checkout.json locator. These methods require no Gest project, issue or author initialization. The source vcs open adapter composes these library methods with locator publication and recovery. Its explicit flags still use the same admission and publisher rules. Root lookup itself only gives authenticated facts and does not recover a locator. Reopen accepts exactly zero or one such catalog4 registration. It independently checks the complete checkout, owner and key inventory against checkout_count, the native root and the supported recording history. Generic private content writes still refuse catalog4.

title: Native local storage
text: This source checkout exposes LocalOwnerRepository::add_files and LocalOwnerRepository::pending_adds, with TrackingLimits and PendingAdd. Call add_files(checkout, paths, wanted, limits, tracking) with the exact CheckoutView from this owner as wanted, plus finite admission and tracking limits. The wanted view states the complete checkout state that the caller expects before mutation. The method validates the whole batch and cumulative inventory, reads and rechecks each regular file, then returns the committed view. The method rejects the batch if the heads, generation, pending version or admission authority are stale. Use the returned view for the next mutation. pending_adds(checkout, limits, tracking) returns the complete bounded pending inventory in pathname order. tracked_paths lists both pending and recorded paths, and path_scopes reads only explicit scope choices. PendingAdd::executable records the mode at first enrollment. Later mode changes do not alter that flag until recording captures the current file. Only this producer’s exact catalog4 state is admitted. New g_vfile rows use the current combined-head vid, or the initial root before recording. They use rid=mrid=0, regular-file link flags, executable mode and observed modification time. A RID is a native artifact row identifier. New batches retain earlier rows and advance pending_version once. Existing-only batches recheck files but change no state. g_pending_path remains empty. New paths have no g_path_scope row, and add preserves earlier explicit choices. Catalog1 rules remain unchanged. No file bytes, canonical artifacts, receipts or file-containing check-ins are stored by add. Working bytes remain unchanged. TrackingLimits bounds the complete inventory and batch count, bytes per path, path components, initial captured working bytes and read buffer size. The final recheck temporarily retains another copy of one captured file. The captured-byte limit therefore does not bound total process memory. The methods reject zero structural or buffer bounds. Capture, recapture and comparison also charge the operation’s borrowed content budget, including retained parent-directory checks. The cumulative work bounds do not measure all process allocations. Captured bytes exist only for transaction validation. Paths and descriptor identities must satisfy the CLI path contract. The protected database identities come from the store’s retained private FileIdentity; callers cannot supply replacement authority. New additions have unselected scope. An absent scope row means neither shared nor private. Add alone authorizes no recording or sync.

title: Native local storage
text: Call initialize, register_checkout, add_files, select_path_scopes, then commit_private_tracked_files. Registration, add, scope selection and changed recording return checkout views. Pass the most recent returned view as the expected view and set request.scope to PathScope::Private. The storage API gives the exact signatures. Supply finite AdmissionLimits for content and parsing, plus TrackingLimits for path counts, path sizes and retained working bytes. Private recording saves the current bytes and executable modes of every tracked file as one complete private history snapshot. Scope is each path’s explicit shared or private choice. Private means owner-local history; shared marks a path for shared history, whose recording and synchronization are not supported here. Every tracked path must have private scope before this recorder can run. The library checkpoint has passed its recorded checks; the CLI checkpoint still needs final qualification. The examples describe source contracts and establish no release or installation. See development status for the accepted tracking baseline and remaining work. select_path_scopes(checkout, wanted, selections, limits, tracking) persists immutable explicit choices for tracked paths. An equal batch is a checked no-op; a conflicting choice rejects the whole batch. A batch with new choices advances pending_version once. path_scopes reads only explicit choices; tracked_paths returns the complete ordered tracked inventory. Neither read infers missing scopes. commit_private_tracked_files(checkout, request, limits, tracking) requires PathScope::Private and a nonempty, duplicate-free set of all tracked paths. It rejects an empty path set, including when the checkout has no tracked paths. Each path must have a persisted private choice. request.expected supplies all seven CheckoutView fields. They are repository ID, checkout ID, registered root, shared head, combined head, generation and pending version. Stale expectations or failed owner validation cause the transaction to reject the request. Catalog1 stores loose private content bytes without a file tree. Catalog4 recording stores a complete file tree and its admitted history. The request supplies actor, comment and native date bytes. The actor is nonempty UTF-8 without NUL. The comment is UTF-8 with no NUL or literal left bracket. Fossil’s comment format uses left brackets to start links. Excluding them keeps the backlink table outside this bounded family. No alternative escape for a literal left bracket is supported. The date must use the native date grammar and be strictly later than every parent, including under native SQL date conversion. The recorder captures all working files again, retaining their bytes and executable modes within finite limits. Edits after add are included without a second add. Capture and parser helpers borrow one content budget and one parser work ledger, which count cumulative work across the whole operation. A request explicitly supplies all tracked paths and the current view: use gossil::storage::{CheckoutView, PathScope, PrivateRecordingRequest}; fn request ( view: &'a CheckoutView, paths: &'a [&'a str], // Every tracked path, not a selected subset. ) -> PrivateRecordingRequest  { PrivateRecordingRequest { expected: view, paths, scope: PathScope::Private, actor: b"Owner", comment: b"Save notes", date: b"2026-11-20T12:00:01", } } Select private scope first. Use a date later than the root and previous private recording. Pass the request to commit_private_tracked_files with explicit limits. Call the initial shared empty root S and private recordings L1, L2 and so on. For example, recording edited notes creates L2 while S stays the shared view. The shared empty root S remains immutable. The first private manifest L1 has parent S; later manifests have parents Lprev then S. Every private manifest contains the complete tree. Keeping S as a parent preserves the explicit shared base while the first parent follows private history. Admission validates the full history and exact native and local projections, including private content, parent, event, leaf, file-link and checkout facts. Later additions use the current combined-head RID as their vid. A projection is a derived database row. Admission rejects a file link whose content hash differs from the hash in its manifest. Catalog4 recording accepts full compressed content and refuses physical deltas. Catalog1 retains its separate delta reconstruction contract. Content that already exists is verified and reused without rewriting its receipt or privacy class. General removal and rename remain unsupported. Recorded.native_name is the new manifest/check-in hash. Recorded also returns the refreshed view after checked commit. NoChange validates metadata, dates, bytes and modes but creates no receipt and changes no head or counter. Changed recording writes one local receipt, payloads, manifest and projections atomically. It advances both generation and pending version once. Working files remain unchanged. Shared recording and synchronization remain unsupported. Catalog1 content operations keep their separate contract. The source CLI exposes scope selection and private recording and inspects recorded states through status. A failed write of the CLI receipt to standard output leaves the recorded history durable.

title: Native local storage
text: LocalOwnerRepository::create installs catalog1, exclusively creates the database file and binds its repository, owner and checkout identities. The initial root contains native C, D, R, T, U and Z records. The parser validates those bytes with date conversion on the same owned SQL connection. Creation installs all six accepted schema files, native markers, compressed root content, native crosslinks, owner, checkout and public receipt together. The final complete-policy marker follows those writes. A failed creation rolls back the schema writes. Root construction computes the encoded user length and complete canonical length before allocating either output. The size calculation and encoder use the same existing token escape rules. Private decoding boundaries check fully stepped native date values and owned catalog fields. A failure rolls back earlier writes in the transaction. Metadata errors preserve the underlying operating-system cause. LocalOwnerRepository::open requires an existing readable and writable regular file. Its explicit AdmissionLimits bound root reconstruction and parsing. For the bound catalog1 constructor, admission checks canonical bytes, native branch tags and event, the public receipt, checkout bindings, complete policy and native versions. The receipt must identify the root itself with validation class local-explicit-publication. The event fields and both branch tags must match the canonical root, including absent event overrides. Admission rejects native or valid typed projections that claim the empty root produces another artifact type or requires a graph dependency. It also rejects current file, merge, path-selection and journal rows outside the empty checkout. A producer identifies the artifact that creates a fact. A target identifies what a fact refers to. Admission distinguishes those roles rather than rejecting every row that mentions the root. In catalog1, operational and provenance rows, invalid diagnostic records and historical selection records can remain. Unrelated private blobs and physical deltas can remain, including a private delta whose baseline is the public root. These rows do not extend the supported public graph or implement their corresponding product operations. AdmissionLimits bound content reconstruction and parser work. Catalog1 admission validates its root; catalog4 admission also checks the complete supported history and charges retained metadata to the same operation budget. Fixed scalar conflict queries bound the data they return. Neither mechanism sets a ceiling on SQLite scan work across stored tables. Operating-system access establishes the local owner boundary. A stored owner ID is a binding, and callers cannot turn an ID string into permission. shared_view() returns a restricted local view with no owner operations. Network authentication and team principals remain unimplemented. The shared view reads the initial public root only. An absent name and a private file name return the same unavailable error. A private association with already public root bytes preserves their public classification. A receipt for an unsupported general graph cannot grant shared access.

title: Native local storage
text: Admission is the validation required before repository operations. A sealed admission proof records SQLite data_version, connection total_changes and exact durable authority metadata. Each content operation checks that proof under its writer reservation before a private lookup. The saved metadata includes the root-conflict predicates. Refreshing only the connection counter cannot accept a newly contradictory projection. An unrelated external commit conservatively requires explicit readmission. Unexpected writes on the same connection also require readmission. In catalog1, supported private file operations refresh only total_changes after checked commit or rollback. They preserve the admitted root and policy, and they never advance the saved data_version. Future root or policy mutation APIs must invalidate or replace the proof after full validation. Content operations do not decode the root through a hidden admission budget. They check durable authority and charge requested content to caller limits. Creation and open use their separate, explicit admission limits.

title: Native local storage
text: For a bound catalog1 repository, use put_private_file_content to store private bytes. Use read_content to retrieve content through LocalOwnerRepository. Every content read or write receives finite Limits. Those limits bound each stored envelope, decoded output, chain depth and aggregate stored and decoded work. Reconstruction checks every intermediate native size and full hash. A RID is a native artifact row identifier. A visited-RID set rejects cycles. A phantom is an artifact whose content is missing. Shunned artifacts are excluded by repository policy. Missing, phantom and shunned baselines reject successful reconstruction. The four-byte big-endian envelope retains native codec behavior. Excess capacity and bytes after the first complete zlib stream are accepted. Exact repository size and hash still have to match. A short NoPayload result cannot stand in for valid empty content. compression::pack_bounded uses the existing encoder and checks the full stored length before each output reservation. Its ceiling includes the header. The encoder also uses a fixed 8192-byte working buffer and backend state. The ceiling is not a bound on every allocation in the process. A hash, policy, codec, schema or resource error makes the borrowed owner rollback-only. Catching the error cannot permit later SQL or successful commit. Earlier writes in that transaction also roll back. Full bytes can replace a phantom or a delta target whose old baseline is missing. Replacement removes the stale delta row and clears phantom state. Typed dependents are records in the adapter projections that require the content. Required orphan, delta or typed dependents cause an explicit refusal until their native and typed crosslinks are implemented.

title: Native local storage
text: LocalOwnerRepository::recorded_timeline(checkout, limits) returns a complete Vec  for an explicit existing catalog4 checkout. Each row has hash: String, date: Vec , actor: Vec , comment: Vec  and private: bool. The generated Rust API gives the exact signature. Results start with the current private check-in and follow its ancestors to the immutable shared empty root S. The root occurs exactly once, last, with private == false; every private row has private == true. Before any private recording, S is the sole row. The reader follows ancestry rather than sorting rows by date. Accepted recordings have strictly increasing dates; equal or backward dates still refuse admission. Hashes are full verified native identities. Dates preserve native D-card bytes; actor and comment preserve the decoded native U-card and C-card bytes exactly. The supported metadata is UTF-8 without NUL, but these public fields remain byte vectors. The reader does not normalize dates, abbreviate hashes or use edited display metadata. Complete native equality admission first authenticates the original event user and comment. Only then does the reader get their owned bytes in the same transaction. One content budget and one parser ledger cover freshness, complete repository admission, metadata queries and result retention. The complete result capacity is charged before allocation. Full admission retains every existing authority, provider, foreign-key, registration, native-root and history projection check. Existing admission callers keep their checks and accounting unchanged. Success returns the entire ancestry only after checked transaction completion. There is no truncation or successful empty history. Missing checkout, stale authority, unsupported or corrupt state, invalid or exhausted limits, allocation, provider and transaction failures return StorageError. The first operation cause and separate cleanup failure retain their existing precedence. This operation reads no working-file contents, makes no durable mutation and publishes no locator. Pending additions and dirty or deleted working files do not change its recorded result. The source timeline and log commands expose this reader as complete compact NDJSON. Existing-locator opening admission is separate from the API operation. Serialization has a third finite allowance derived from the unchanged CLI decoded-content limit. No whole-invocation aggregate budget is claimed. Revision selection, filters and broader Fossil timeline behavior remain deferred.

title: Native local storage
text: Each catalog installs six SQL inputs under src/storage/schema/. Catalog4 substitutes adapter-catalog4.sql for the catalog1 adapter. The required object inventory and complete stored definitions are checked before mutation. Known optional schema families return an unsupported configuration error. Unregistered persistent triggers receive a separate error. Dynamic ticket templates, extension schemas and their registry transitions remain unimplemented. General public receipts, publication, native and typed rebuild, retained-dependency administration and filesystem journals also remain unimplemented. The public APIs do not offer those operations.

title: Native local storage
text: Prefer initialize, then register_checkout when one native empty-root registration is needed. Use create for catalog1 private content operations. For private recording, select scopes explicitly and pass the latest complete view and every tracked path to the library recorder. Set finite admission limits, then consult the generated API for repository creation, admission and content methods.

title: Emit a task creation artifact
text: The task_ticket module turns a validated TaskValues snapshot into complete, uncompressed bytes in Fossil’s ticket artifact format. A ticket records work to track, and its artifact is a sequence of newline-terminated records called cards. Gossil uses those cards to carry task fields. Here, native means the Fossil artifact format. Use the library to inspect or test task creation artifacts in memory. No current Gossil repository API consumes these bytes. Raw input admission, storage integration and issue commands remain separate work.

title: Emit a task creation artifact
text: Validate all eleven decoded fields with task_from_values first. The task values guide shows that step. Given the resulting task, emit an artifact with an explicit byte limit: use gossil::native_date::NativeDate; use gossil::task_ticket::task_creation_bytes; let date = NativeDate::parse(b"2026-11-18T12:00:00.000000001Z").unwrap(); let ticket_id = b"0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567"; let bytes = task_creation_bytes(&task, ticket_id, b"native actor", date, 65_536).unwrap(); assert!(bytes.len() <= 65_536); Use the application setup when calling Gossil from another crate. Handle DateError and TicketError in applications rather than unwrapping the results. A J card assigns a named field to its encoded value. The D card records the artifact creation date, and the U card records its actor. The K card contains the native ticket identity, which requires exactly forty lowercase ASCII hexadecimal bytes. Supply it independently of the task’s gest_id. Gest is a task and artifact tracker. A Gest ID has 32 lowercase letters from k through z and remains a J field. The emitter neither generates identities nor derives one identity from the other. The U card contains caller-supplied actor bytes escaped with the Fossil token codec. These bytes need not be a Gest author ID or UTF-8 text.

title: Emit a task creation artifact
text: NativeDate represents a Gregorian UTC instant as signed i128 nanoseconds since the Unix epoch. Supported years are 0001 through 9999, inclusive. parse accepts YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS[.fraction][Z], where a fraction has one through nine digits. A missing suffix also means UTC. It rejects offsets, leap seconds, year zero, invalid calendars and excess fractional digits. It does not normalize other spellings into this grammar. from_epoch_nanos checks the same year range. epoch_nanos returns the integer value without floating-point conversion. Display and the emitted D card use exactly nine fractional digits and no suffix. This domain is separate from the more permissive Gest business timestamps in TaskValues. The caller supplies the D card date independently of those timestamps.

title: Emit a task creation artifact
text: The artifact has a D card, fourteen J cards sorted by field name, a K card, a U card and a final Z checksum card. Each card ends with a newline. The eleven model fields are assigned_to, created_at, description, gest_id, metadata, priority, project_id, resolved_at, status, title and updated_at. Each uses compact serde_json encoding of the values returned by task_to_values, followed by native token escaping. Strings retain JSON quotes, priority is an integer or null, and metadata retains its JSON value. Status and business timestamps use the normalized forms in the task values contract. Null values remain present. The three fixed fields classify this Gossil record. gossil_deleted is JSON false, marking the creation as not deleted. gossil_kind is raw task, identifying a task record, and gossil_schema is raw 1, identifying its schema version. These fields define Gossil’s task schema; this emitter does not implement a consumer for that schema. The last two values are literal bytes rather than JSON strings. This function emits complete creation snapshots. It emits neither field-appending updates that extend existing field values nor cards that link a parent artifact to record ancestry. See the artifact parser guide for supported structural card forms. The Z card holds the lowercase MD5 checksum of all preceding artifact bytes. max_output bounds the complete encoded artifact, including token expansion, card syntax, checksum and newlines. The effective limit also respects isize::MAX. An exact-size limit succeeds; a smaller limit returns TicketError::Size. The limit is an output bound, rather than a total heap budget. The emitter counts borrowed model values before retaining serialized JSON or reserving the output buffer. Bookkeeping allocations have fixed bounds independent of task string and metadata sizes. Timestamp formatting, the fourteen-field list and the checksum still allocate. Even a zero output limit can therefore allocate fixed bookkeeping; the limit does not cap all memory use. TicketError::TicketId rejects malformed K bytes. Allocation retains a fallible reservation error, Token retains a token codec error, and Json retains a serialization error. The generated API documents these variants.

title: Emit a task creation artifact
text: Check raw field presence, duplicate keys and input byte limits before constructing TaskValues. Choose the native ticket identity, actor, D instant and output budget independently of the task’s model fields. The emitter performs no clock reads, identity generation or database writes. It does not replay history, check references to other records or determine who may write a task. A future repository operation must define and enforce those rules, including any requirement that artifact dates increase. Emission alone does not establish Fossil engine compatibility. Repository migration must separately validate and store any existing records. This page follows the nossaifd writing guide, including principles credited to Rosalind Reid, Shreya Shankar and Oskar Austegard.

title: Emit a task creation artifact
text: Use task_from_values to validate a snapshot, then call task_creation_bytes with an explicit output limit. Next, inspect the returned bytes or use them in application tests, and handle emission errors. Repository storage integration remains planned.

title: Fossil token bytes
text: API: fossilize gives the exact contract. The gossil::token_codec module encodes and decodes arbitrary bytes for Fossil artifact and protocol tokens. It implements the token escape functions from Fossil revision b3a1c8efb2731dffbd5cc38c58ac349746de6da6, src/encode.c:392-458. It does not parse artifacts or select repository hash policy.

title: Fossil token bytes
text: All three functions return Result and preserve allocation error causes. fossilize encodes the entire slice, including embedded NUL bytes. fossilize_c_string encodes bytes before the first NUL, or the whole slice when no NUL occurs. Both return bytes without a C terminator. The eight escaped bytes are NUL, space, tab, newline, carriage return, vertical tab, form feed and backslash. Their escape letters are 0, s, t, n, r, v, f and backslash. Each follows a backslash. Other bytes pass through unchanged. No function requires UTF-8. defossilize stops reading at the first source NUL or the slice end. Unknown escapes discard the backslash. For example, \q decodes to q. A terminal backslash survives. The returned DecodedToken.bytes contains every emitted byte, including bytes emitted after a decoded NUL. Its c_string_len is the first decoded NUL index, or the output length. C-string consumers see only that prefix. use gossil::token_codec::{defossilize, fossilize}; let encoded = fossilize(b"a b\0").unwrap(); let decoded = defossilize(&encoded).unwrap(); assert_eq!(decoded.bytes, b"a b\0"); assert_eq!(decoded.c_string_len, 3); The implementation checks the exact encoded size and reserves output storage before emitting bytes. TokenError::Size rejects arithmetic overflow or lengths above Rust vector capacity. TokenError::Allocation retains the allocator error. These errors are Rust resource policies. The C comparison requires valid pointers, terminated C strings and explicit lengths within allocated storage. It excludes signed C integer overflow and allocation exhaustion.

title: Fossil token bytes
text: Use the contracts above with explicit resource limits. Next, consult the generated Rust API for the full signatures and errors.

title: Working with repositories
text: Use this guide to plan which agent files to track, how to review changes, and how to connect tasks to exact file versions. Plan the history around a task, its plan and the evidence behind a decision. Git remains the source-code authority. Gossil is designed to give the surrounding agent work its own history and sharing rules. Most of this page describes planned repository workflows. The source CLI supports empty repository initialization and three file-delta diagnostics. Initialization creates no checkout and selects no files. The source vcs open command registers one checkout at the empty root, or reopens it with supported private history and locator recovery. The source also supports explicit tracking, scope selection and private recording. Its Rust library implements the corresponding storage contracts. Library registration selects no files and publishes no locator, the local file that lets commands find and verify a checkout. Catalog1 private content operations follow their separate native storage contract. The private recording library saves the complete tracked tree within the resource limits in its storage contract. It does not provide shared recording or issue management. The Fossil references teach the inherited workflow; their commands are not Gossil aliases.

title: Working with repositories
text:
A separately installed development preview supports a small local file workflow. This unmerged preview is not a release, and full qualification is incomplete. Use a disposable folder and copies of files, and keep Git as the source authority. These commands require that preview’s installed gos or gossil executable. The source CLI supports init, native open, add, status, scope and private commit with the explicit source grammar. Its timeline and log grammar differs from the preview. It accepts neither --limit nor --json. The source also rejects the preview’s commit grammar and has no diff command. The generated Rust API on this site does not describe the preview’s additional storage methods. Start with an empty scratch checkout. Keep the repository database outside it: trial=$(mktemp -d /tmp/gossil-preview.XXXXXX) mkdir -p "$trial/work/app/.agent" "$trial/work/service/.agent" gos vcs init "$trial/history.gossil" gos vcs open --repository "$trial/history.gossil" --checkout source --root "$trial/work" printf 'first plan
' > "$trial/work/app/.agent/plan.md" printf 'first review
' > "$trial/work/service/.agent/review.md" gos vcs add --repository "$trial/history.gossil" --checkout source --path app/.agent/plan.md service/.agent/review.md gos vcs status --repository "$trial/history.gossil" --checkout source --json gos vcs commit --repository "$trial/history.gossil" --checkout source -m "Record agent files" The folders can sit below sibling Git repositories. Gossil tracks the explicitly named paths independently of Git’s index. Here, add chooses paths for tracking; it is not Git-style content staging for each later commit. Edit a tracked file, inspect the change and commit again without re-adding it: printf 'revised plan
' > "$trial/work/app/.agent/plan.md" gos vcs status --repository "$trial/history.gossil" --checkout source --json gos vcs diff --repository "$trial/history.gossil" --checkout source --path app/.agent/plan.md gossil vcs commit --repository "$trial/history.gossil" --checkout source -m "Revise the plan" gos vcs timeline --repository "$trial/history.gossil" --checkout source --limit 10 --json gossil vcs log --repository "$trial/history.gossil" --checkout source --limit 10 --json gos vcs open --repository "$trial/history.gossil" --checkout source A recording commit includes changed tracked paths; these examples do not request a partial commit. log is the alias for timeline. Reopening an existing checkout omits --root; it does not restore or replace working files. No issue, project or author initialization is required for this file workflow. The installed preview passed an isolated smoke test covering the initial empty check-in, two later commits and reopen. This result does not establish release readiness, branching, sync, automatic checkout discovery or full Fossil parity. Issue commands and the server remain unavailable in the preview.

title: Working with repositories
text: In the planned workflow, an agent revises a tracked plan, updates its task and retains a private trace. Review the file diff and task changes together before requesting the integrated operation. The operation checks expected revisions and commits artifacts, derived records, scope, local command history and Gossil checkout heads together. Record-only work creates no file check-in. The shared head selects shared files. An optional private combined head contains those files with the same bytes and attributes, plus selected private files. Each checkout stores its own head pair. Historical review chooses a permitted file head and the exact contributing artifact sets for issues and discussions. Two task-only edits can share one file head, so a check-in hash does not select an issue revision. Complete references also retain required notes, link targets and discussion dependencies. Later arrivals do not rewrite that historical set. Typed issue-to-code links support navigation in both directions across registered Git repositories. They pin commits, blobs and any selected ranges or changes; current filenames and moving branch names cannot supply that guarantee. Required captures preserve permitted target bytes when external code is absent. A descriptor is a structured record naming the versioned target and any selected range. Its transferable encoding remains unfinished; there is no exchange format for applications to implement from this guide yet. Fossil already has immutable ticket history and file check-ins. Gossil’s added contract coordinates exact record boundaries, shared/private file heads and scoped links. Gest contributes the task workflow; one owned transaction strengthens its multi-statement storage helpers. This coordinated operation is planned and is not provided by the current delta diagnostics. The transaction commits changes to the Gossil database. Git commits remain separate source operations, and checkout files are materialized after commit with recovery bookkeeping. A failure then can require checkout recovery while the database history remains committed. Ordinary commands do not automatically combine unrelated file and issue work. See library concepts for the shared model and compare Gossil with Git for the plan/task example and current availability.

title: Working with repositories
section: Separate stored history from the files you edit
text: A repository holds recorded history. A checkout is the folder of files you edit at a selected point in that history. A check-in records a file tree, its parent versions and a comment. A file you edit in the checkout has not become a new check-in until you commit it. Fossil’s concepts guide explains this separation. An artifact is immutable content identified by a hash. A manifest records which file paths and content hashes belong to a check-in. A delta encodes bytes for storage or transfer. It is not itself a user-visible history entry, so the delta tutorial creates no repository history. For Gossil, plan one local repository database with both private and shared material. A team replica receives the shared portion. You do not need a separate personal repository to keep private agent notes. Team replication remains planned.

title: Working with repositories
section: Choose the checkout root and tracked files
text: Choose a root above all the agent files you want in one history. That root may contain several Git repositories. For example, the intended selection could look like this: workspace/ Gossil checkout root AGENTS.md selected by Gossil app/ Git repository src/main.rs selected by Git .agent/plan.md selected by Gossil service/ another Git repository .agent/review.md selected by Gossil The two systems choose files independently. A Git ignore rule for .agent/ does not select those files for Gossil, and Git’s index does not define Gossil’s tracked set. The intended tracking model also permits a Gossil root inside a Git checkout. Choose the root to fit the paths you need. Gossil operations must preserve the nested Git indices, branches and commits. Initialization is intended to select no files automatically. Select files explicitly, then inspect the pending selection before making a check-in. Keep these states distinct: File state Meaning Tracked Selected for version control; edits can enter later check-ins Untracked Present on disk but outside the selected file history Ignored Matches a rule that helps omit unmanaged paths from discovery or recursive addition Missing A tracked path is absent on disk; inspect whether removal was intended An ignore rule is a selection aid, not permission control. Fossil treats explicit paths differently from recursive addition. Recursive addition normally omits dotfiles, while explicitly named ignored files can require confirmation or force. See its add reference. Gossil’s planned default ignore pattern is .git,*/.git,.git/*,*/.git/*. It excludes Git metadata, including .git directories and Git worktree .git files. It must still be possible to see what was selected. The preset does not protect private content by itself.

title: Working with repositories
section: Review a change before recording it
text: The intended daily file workflow follows Fossil: Inspect status to identify edited, added, missing, removed and renamed paths. Read the diff to inspect the actual changes in tracked files. Add new paths, record intentional removals, and record renames. Review status and diff again, then commit one coherent change with a comment. Inspect history to find the resulting check-in and its parent versions. In Fossil, status describes pending changes, while diff compares content. Inspect untracked files separately. A quiet diff of tracked files does not prove that every intended file was added. A commit records the pending changes, unless a file subset was requested. The timeline helps locate earlier work. Removing a path from future versions does not erase its older history. Also distinguish recording a removal or rename from changing the file on disk. Fossil’s remove and move commands have options and settings that control disk effects. Check those effects before using Fossil itself. Gossil will need its own command reference when these operations ship.

title: Working with repositories
text: A branch names a line of check-ins. A fork occurs when work produces competing tips on the same branch. For a plan experiment, a named branch lets you keep the experiment separate while retaining its starting point. See Fossil’s branching guide. Merging combines changes in the checkout. Inspect the result, resolve conflicts and test the affected work before committing the merge. Fossil’s merge reference makes that separate commit step explicit. Downloading another check-in and merging it into your files are different decisions. Gossil’s branches and merge operations remain planned; use your existing Git workflow for source-code work now.

title: Working with repositories
section: Distinguish sharing history from updating a checkout
text: Fossil gives four useful names to repository transfer operations: Operation Purpose in Fossil Clone Create a local repository from an existing one Pull Receive remote history into the local repository Push Send local history to another repository Sync Exchange history in both directions A clone and an open checkout are distinct operations, even where Fossil offers to do both together. A pull receives history. Updating the checkout changes the files you work on. See the clone reference and sharing section. Fossil’s autosync setting can arrange transfers around commands such as commit and update. Know which remote and mode you are using before assuming a local action was shared. Gossil plans to retain replication and autosync workflows, but none of these transfer operations is currently a Gossil command. Gossil adds an explicit private/shared boundary. The planned local write can record a shared issue change and private notes in one database transaction. Either both changes commit or both roll back. Shared history must remain usable without private dependencies. To publish shared material, it is not enough to omit some paths during transfer. The planned synchronization rules define that boundary. Neither an ignore pattern nor Fossil’s private-transfer options establish that Gossil contract.

title: Working with repositories
section: Connect tasks to exact file versions
text: A task describes the work, and a file check-in records selected files. Updating an issue does not have to create a new file check-in. Fossil stores ticket changes as separate artifacts, as its ticket guide explains. Gest is a task and artifact tracker. Gossil adapts this history model to Gest’s tasks, projects and related records. When you record why a change was made, name the exact version. The planned Gossil file reference contains a check-in, relative path and content hash. A Git file reference names its registered repository, full commit, path and blob. A moving branch name alone cannot identify the version an agent read. Uncommitted content needs a captured snapshot if the reference must survive later edits. Exact version references are part of the planned issue and annotation model. A Git object reference also does not guarantee that a recipient has its bytes. The current task, project and author converters validate decoded records in memory. They do not save an issue or create a file reference. Their generated API links give the callable surface. Notebook support remains planned. A notebook is a selected directory and its tracked descendants. It is intended to use selected native file history. SQLAR packages, which are SQLite archives of files, are for interchange rather than a second history system.

title: Working with repositories
text: Before discarding work, inspect the affected paths and keep any unsaved material you still need. Restoring files, backing out a recorded change and undoing a task command have different effects. In Fossil, revert restores files to the checkout baseline or a requested revision. With no file argument it acts on all files. Undo can reverse certain recent working-tree operations, including update, merge and revert. It has one level; commit and checkout clear it. Its dry-run option shows what it would restore. It is not a general backup or an undo for every command. Gossil’s intended undo for Gest command history is separate from undo for operations on checkout files. General recovery commands are not available in the current CLI. For today’s delta diagnostics, preserve the inputs and write to a new output path. Compare the restored bytes before replacing a file.

title: Working with repositories
text: The add and status commands track exact paths and show pending additions or recorded paths with their actual scope. Add stores no file bytes. New paths remain unselected until vcs scope or a library caller makes an explicit scope choice. The private recording API requires immutable private scope for every tracked path. Supply the complete tracked set and the latest checkout view. It rereads all current bytes and executable modes, including changes made since add, and records one complete private snapshot. The shared empty root stays unchanged. An identical tree is a checked no-op, and recording never modifies working files. Use the source walkthrough for explicit scope selection, private commit, edits without re-add and reopen. The separate preview above has a different command contract. Consult development status before assuming that a source feature is installed or released. For a stored history view, library callers can use recorded_timeline. It returns the complete current-first ancestry, including the shared root last. Pending additions and dirty or deleted working files do not alter these records. The source timeline and log commands print those records as compact NDJSON. They require both explicit selectors and a complete matching locator. Their grammar differs from the installed preview above. They accept neither --limit nor --json. These source commands supply no new evidence about the installed preview or its reopen behavior.

Continue to pass exact paths to add and scope commands. The focused source checkpoint passed its recorded controls; complete delivery qualification and the installed development preview are separate.

Duplicate separators collapse to one, but an initial double slash stays. The function removes a leading ./, each internal /./ and each /component/.. that can cancel. Unresolved .. components stay, even above an absolute root. As in native Fossil, a nonempty name whose simplified bytes are empty becomes /. A relative name that cancels past its start, such as a/.., is a relative terminal cancellation. It leaves native C with a negative cursor and a terminator outside the buffer, and this function rejects it. The input buffer holds at most max_input_bytes plus one sentinel byte. The output bound applies to the actual length of the simplified name.

title: file_path
text: source pub fn simplify_name_for_source( input: &[u8], keep_trailing_slash: bool, limits: Limits, platform: SourcePlatform, ) -> Result  Simplify a filename by the branch of the Fossil source that the caller selects. The Windows/Cygwin branch converts every backslash to a slash. Then it removes //?/ and compares the next three bytes with UNC, by the ASCII case map of SQLite. The function does not check drives, the names after the UNC prefix or whether a name is valid. For the input //?/, native C copies the terminator of the input to byte zero but reports a length of one. So the result keeps that NUL in its reported span, and its visible C string is empty. The input buffer holds at most the length of the input plus one sentinel byte. The output bound counts the reported span, with any NUL inside that span. After the loops compact the name, the native lookahead can still read the original bytes at the end of the buffer. A relative terminal cancellation returns the same error as simplify_name.

text: Returns PathError for an exceeded bound, a NUL, a failed allocation or a relative terminal cancellation.

The list ends at its first NUL; no escape syntax is applied.

text: source pub fn glob_expr(value: &[u8], list: Option , limits: Limits) -> Result , GlobError> Build a SQL expression from trusted SQL and Fossil patterns, with native quote advancement. The caller MUST supply a trusted SQL value expression. Only pattern apostrophes are escaped; value is neither quoted nor sanitized. Never pass untrusted SQL. Use a trusted column or parameter expression such as b"?1" and bind candidate bytes separately when executing the result through a caller-owned SQL interface. This function executes no SQL. All input slices end at their first NUL. Empty, absent and delimiter-only lists return b"0"; a quoted empty pattern produces a real GLOB term. Adjacent text after a closing quote can therefore differ from glob_create and glob_multi_match parsing.

text: source pub fn task_creation_bytes( task: &TaskValues, ticket_id: &[u8], actor: &[u8], date: NativeDate, max_output: usize, ) -> Result , TicketError> Emit complete uncompressed Fossil ticket artifact bytes for a validated task creation. The caller supplies the K card’s ticket identity, actor bytes and a validated creation date. K is forty lowercase ASCII hexadecimal bytes, independent of the 32-character Gest ID in the task. Actor bytes need not be UTF-8 or a Gest author ID. crate::gest_task_values supplies the normalized status spelling and UTC timestamp strings. All eleven model fields use JSON followed by native token escaping. The three additional J fields are gossil_deleted=false, raw gossil_kind=task and raw gossil_schema=1. The fourteen J fields are sorted by name. No append or parent card is emitted. The caller manages history and enforces any requirement that artifact creation dates increase. max_output bounds complete encoded bytes, including the final checksum and newline, with an effective ceiling of isize::MAX. It is not a heap budget. The emitter counts token-escaped JSON bytes before retaining serialized JSON or reserving output bytes.
